title.zh: 卷五十六 列傳第二十六 江統 孫楚
title.en: Volume 56 Biographies 26: Jiang Tong; Sun Chu
title.raw: 卷五十六 列傳第二十六 江統 孫楚 Volume 56 Biographies 26: Jiang Tong; Sun Chu

sentences.zh: 江統 子虨、惇 孫楚 孫統、綽

translations.literal: Jiang Tong; sons Bin and Dun. Sun Chu; sons Tong and Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Tong, with his sons Jiang Bin and Jiang Dun; Sun Chu, with his sons Sun Tong and Sun Chuo.

sentences.zh: 江統，字應元，陳留圉人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Tong, courtesy name Yingyuan, was a man of Yu in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Tong, whose courtesy name was Yingyuan, came from Yu in Chenliu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖蕤，以義行稱，為譙郡太守，封亢父男。

translations.literal: His grandfather Rui was famed for righteous conduct, served as governor of Qiao commandery, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Kangfu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jiang Rui was celebrated for principled conduct, rose to governor of Qiao commandery, and received the noble title of Baron of Kangfu.

sentences.zh: 父祚，南安太守。

translations.literal: His father Zuo was governor of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiang Zuo served as governor of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 統靜默有遠志，時人為之語曰：「嶷然稀言江應元。

translations.literal: Tong was quiet and reserved and had lofty aims; people of the time made a saying for him, saying, "Grave and seldom speaking—Jiang Yingyuan."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Tong was reserved in manner and nursed far-reaching ambitions; his contemporaries coined a saying: "Stately and sparing of words—that is Jiang Yingyuan."

sentences.zh: 」與鄉人蔡克俱知名。

translations.literal: " Together with his fellow townsman Cai Ke he was both well known.
translations.idiomatic: " He and his townsman Cai Ke were celebrated together.

sentences.zh: 襲父爵，除山陰令。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's noble rank and was appointed magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to his father's title and was appointed magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 時關隴、屢為氐、羌所擾，孟觀西討，自擒氐帥齊萬年。

translations.literal: At that time Guan and Long were repeatedly disturbed by the Di and Qiang; Meng Guan campaigned west and personally captured the Di chieftain Qi Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Guanzhong and Longxi region was repeatedly harried by Di and Qiang forces; Meng Guan led a western expedition and personally took the Di leader Qi Wannian prisoner.

sentences.zh: 統深惟四夷亂華，宜杜其萌，乃作《徙戎論》。

translations.literal: Tong deeply reflected that the four barbarians disordering Huaxia ought to be stopped at the sprout, and therefore composed the "Discourse on Relocating the Rong."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Tong reflected deeply that when frontier peoples throw the Chinese heartland into turmoil, the evil must be cut off at the root; he therefore wrote his treatise "On Relocating the Rong."

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its words said:
translations.idiomatic: The text runs as follows:

sentences.zh: 夫夷蠻戎狄，謂之四夷，九服之制，地在要荒。

translations.literal: The Yi, Man, Rong, and Di are called the four barbarians; in the system of the nine domains, their lands lie in Yao and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern Yi, southern Man, western Rong, and northern Di are grouped as the "four barbarians"; under the classical scheme of the nine concentric domains, their territories fall in the outer rings of Yao and Huang.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》之義，內諸夏而外夷狄。

translations.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn is to take the various Xia within and the Yi and Di without.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals teach that the Chinese states are to be cherished within, while the barbarian peoples are to be kept outside.

sentences.zh: 以其言語不通，贄幣不同，法俗詭異，種類乖殊；

translations.literal: Because their speech is not mutually intelligible, their tribute goods are not the same, their laws and customs are strange and different, and their kinds are divergent;
translations.idiomatic: Their languages do not mesh, their ritual offerings differ, law and custom are alien, and their stocks are wholly unlike our own;

sentences.zh: 或居絕域之外，山河之表，崎嶇川穀阻險之地，與中國壤斷土隔，不相侵涉，賦役不及，正朔不加，故曰「天子有道，守在四夷」。

translations.literal: some dwell beyond the farthest regions, beyond mountains and rivers, in rugged river-valleys and obstructed perilous places, with broken soil and severed ground from the Middle Kingdom, not mutually encroaching, corvée and taxes not reaching them, correct calendrical beginning not applied to them; therefore it is said, "When the Son of Heaven has the Way, defense lies with the four barbarians."
translations.idiomatic: some live beyond the rim of the known world, shielded by ranges and rivers, in broken terrain where gorges block the way, cut off from the Central Plains so that neither side trespasses on the other, where no tax or labor levy reaches them and the royal calendar is never imposed—hence the saying, "When the Son of Heaven holds the Way, his defense is entrusted to the four barbarians."

sentences.zh: 禹平九土，而西戎即敘。

translations.literal: Yu pacified the nine soils, and the western Rong thereupon were ordered.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu brought peace to the nine provinces, the western Rong submitted of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 其性氣貪婪，凶悍不仁，四夷之中，戎狄為甚。

translations.literal: Their nature and qi are greedy and cruel, fierce and harsh and not benevolent; among the four barbarians, the Rong and Di are the worst.
translations.idiomatic: They are greedy by temperament, brutal and lacking in human sympathy; among the four kinds of barbarians, the Rong and Di are the most intractable.

sentences.zh: 弱則畏服，強則侵叛。

translations.literal: When weak they fear and submit; when strong they invade and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Weak, they cringe and obey; strong, they raid and break faith.

sentences.zh: 雖有賢聖之世，大德之君，咸未能以通化率導，而以恩德柔懷也。

translations.literal: Although there are ages of worthies and sages, rulers of great virtue, all have been unable by universal transformation to lead and guide them, and by grace and virtue to soften and cherish them.
translations.idiomatic: Even in ages graced with sages and under sovereigns of the highest moral stature, no one has ever truly civilized them through moral example alone, or bound them for long with kindness alone.

sentences.zh: 當其強也，以殷之高宗而憊于鬼方，有周文王而患昆夷、獫狁，高祖困于白登，孝文軍於霸上。

translations.literal: When they were strong, with the Shang's Gaozong one was exhausted by Guifang; with the Zhou's King Wen one had troubles from the Kun Yi and Xianyun; Gaozu was distressed at Baideng; Xiaowen encamped at Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: At their strongest they wore down even King Wuding of Shang against Guifang, troubled King Wen of Zhou with the Kun barbarians and the Xianyun, trapped the Han founder at Baideng, and forced Emperor Wen to camp his host at Bashang.

sentences.zh: 及其弱也，周公來九譯之貢，中宗納單于之朝，以元成之微，而猶四夷賓服。

translations.literal: When they were weak, the Duke of Zhou received tribute through nine interpreters; Zhongzong admitted the Chanyu's court; with the feebleness of Yuan and Cheng, still the four barbarians guest-submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When they weakened, the Duke of Zhou received embassies that passed through nine rounds of translation; Emperor Xuan of Han welcomed the Shanyu to court; and even under the later emperors Yuan and Cheng, whose reigns lacked vigor, the four quarters still came as deferential guests.

sentences.zh: 此其已然之效也。

translations.literal: This is their already realized effect.
translations.idiomatic: History has already shown how this works.

sentences.zh: 故匈奴求守邊塞，而侯應陳其不可，單于屈膝未央，望之議以不臣。

translations.literal: Therefore when the Xiongnu sought to guard the border passes, Hou Ying set forth that it could not be; when the Chanyu bent the knee at Weiyang, Wang Zhi deliberated that he was not to be treated as a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: That is why, when the Xiongnu asked to garrison the frontier for the Han, Hou Ying argued the plan down; and when the Shanyu knelt in homage at Weiyang Palace, Xiao Wangzhi counseled that he must not be accepted as a true subject.

sentences.zh: 是以有道之君牧夷狄也，惟以待之有備，禦之有常，雖稽顙執贄，而邊城不弛固守；

translations.literal: Therefore when a ruler who has the Way herds the Yi and Di, only by treating them with preparedness and defending them with constancy—even though they knock the forehead and hold tribute gifts—does the border city not relax firm defense;
translations.idiomatic: A true king, then, governs the barbarians by keeping them at arm's length and holding a standing defense: even when they press their foreheads to the dust and bear gifts, the garrisons on the frontier never stand down.

sentences.zh: 為寇賊強暴，而兵甲不加遠征，期令境內獲安，疆埸不侵而已。

translations.literal: if they become bandit-thieves, violent and strong, yet armor and weapons are not applied to distant expeditions, the expectation being only to order that within the borders security is obtained and the border fields are not encroached upon.
translations.idiomatic: If they turn to raiding, one does not launch endless punitive expeditions into the steppe; the aim is simply peace inside the realm and an unmolested border.

sentences.zh: 及至周室失統，諸侯專征，以大兼小，轉相殘滅，封疆不固，而利害異心。

translations.literal: When it reached the Zhou house losing its thread, the feudal lords monopolized punitive expeditions, using the large to annex the small, in turn mutually destroying one another, enfeoffed borders not firm, and benefit and harm with different hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Zhou kings lost the reins, the regional lords took war into their own hands, great swallowed small in an endless chain of mutual destruction, frontiers ceased to hold, and each power pursued its own interest.

sentences.zh: 戎狄乘間，得入中國。

translations.literal: The Rong and Di took advantage of the interval and were able to enter the Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: The Rong and Di seized their opening and poured into the Chinese heartland.

sentences.zh: 或招誘安撫，以為己用。

translations.literal: Some summoned and enticed and pacified and soothed them, taking them for their own use.
translations.idiomatic: Some states courted them with blandishments and enrolled them as auxiliaries of their own.

sentences.zh: 故申、繒之禍，顛覆宗周；

translations.literal: Therefore the disaster of Shen and Zeng overturned the ancestral Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Hence the debacle at Shen and Zeng that toppled the house of Zhou;

sentences.zh: 襄公要秦，遽興姜戎。

translations.literal: Duke Xiang made a pact with Qin, and suddenly raised the Jiang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: hence Duke Xiang of Jin's bargain with Qin and the sudden mobilization of the Jiang Rong.

sentences.zh: 當春秋時，義渠、大荔居秦、晉之域，陸渾、陰戎處伊、洛之間，鄋瞞之屬害及濟東，侵入齊、宋，陵虐邢、衛，南夷與北狄交侵中國，不絕若線。

translations.literal: In the time of the Spring and Autumn, Yiqu and Dali dwelled in the territories of Qin and Jin; Luhun and the Yin Rong were located between the Yi and Luo; the Souman types harmed as far as east of Ji, encroached into Qi and Song, oppressed Xing and Wei; southern Yi and northern Di together encroached the Middle Kingdom, unbroken like a thread.
translations.idiomatic: In the Spring and Autumn era the Yiqu and Dali peoples lodged inside Qin and Jin; the Luhun Rong and the Yin Rong camped between the Yi and Luo rivers; Souman and their kind ravaged the country east of the Ji, pushed into Qi and Song, and battered Xing and Wei; southern barbarians and northern Di took turns invading the Central States until the dynasty's life hung by a thread.

sentences.zh: 齊桓攘之，存亡繼絕，北伐山戎，以開燕路。

translations.literal: Huan of Qi repelled them, preserved those perishing and continued those cut off, north campaigned against the Mountain Rong, in order to open the road to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi drove them back, restored ruined states and revived broken successions, marched north against the Mountain Rong, and cleared the way into Yan.

sentences.zh: 故仲尼稱管仲之力，嘉左衽之功。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhongni praised Guan Zhong's force, commended the merit of the left lapel.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius therefore praised Guan Zhong's achievement and spoke with approval of his having spared the Chinese the humiliation of "buttoning the lapel on the left."

sentences.zh: 逮至春秋之末，戰國方盛，楚吞蠻氏，晉翦陸渾，趙武胡服，開榆中之地，秦雄咸陽，滅義渠之等。

translations.literal: Reaching the end of Spring and Autumn, the Warring States just flourished; Chu swallowed the Man clan; Jin extirpated Luhun; King Wuling of Zhao Hu-clothed, opened the lands of Yuzhong; Qin was mighty at Xianyang, extinguished Yiqu and the like.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Spring and Autumn period the Warring States were in full swing: Chu swallowed the Man tribes; Jin wiped out the Luhun Rong; King Wuling of Zhao adopted nomad dress and pushed into the Yuzhong frontier; Qin made Xianyang its seat of power and destroyed Yiqu and similar states.

sentences.zh: 始皇之並天下也，南兼百越，北走匈奴，五嶺長城，戎卒億計。

translations.literal: When the First Emperor annexed all under Heaven, south he combined the Hundred Yue, north he drove the Xiongnu; the five ranges, the long wall, barbarian soldiers in numbers of yi.
translations.idiomatic: When the First Emperor united the realm, he absorbed the Hundred Yue in the south, drove the Xiongnu northward, threw the Five Ridges and the Long Wall across the landscape, and stationed countless frontier troops.

sentences.zh: 雖師役煩殷，寇賊橫暴，然一世之功，戎虜奔卻，當時中國無復四夷也。

translations.literal: Although army service was vexingly abundant, bandit-thieves were violent and cruel, yet in one generation's achievement, the Rong captives ran off and withdrew; at that time in the Middle Kingdom there were again no four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns were endless and marauders still bold, yet in a single reign the northern tribes were thrown back and, for a time, the heartland knew no barbarian powers pressing in on four sides.

sentences.zh: 漢興而都長安，關中之郡號曰三輔，《禹貢》雍州，宗周豐、鎬之舊也。

translations.literal: Han rose and capitalized at Chang'an; the commanderies within the passes were called the Three Adjuncts; in the Tribute of Yu, Yongzhou, the old traces of the ancestral Zhou's Feng and Hao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han rose, it set its capital at Chang'an; the commanderies of Guanzhong were known as the Three Adjuncts—the Yongzhou of the Tribute of Yu, the ancient ground of the Western Zhou capitals Feng and Hao.

sentences.zh: 及至王莽之敗，赤眉因之，西都荒毀，百姓流亡。

translations.literal: When it reached Wang Mang's defeat, the Red Eyebrows followed upon it, the western capital was desolate and destroyed, the hundred surnames fled and wandered.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang's fall brought the Red Eyebrows in his wake; the western capital was left a ruin and the people scattered.

sentences.zh: 建武中，以馬援領隴西太守，討叛羌，徙其餘種于關中，居馮翊、河東空地，而與華人雜處。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu period, because Ma Yuan led as governor of Longxi, punishing the rebel Qiang, he moved their remaining kinds into the passes within, dwelling in the empty lands of Fengyi and Hedong, and mixed dwelling with Huaren.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Guangwu, Ma Yuan, as governor of Longxi, suppressed the rebel Qiang and resettled the surviving tribes inside the passes, on vacant land in Fengyi and Hedong, where they lived intermingled with Chinese subjects.

sentences.zh: 數歲之後，族類蕃息，既恃其肥強，且苦漢人侵之。

translations.literal: After several years, the clans and kinds multiplied and rested; relying on their fatness and strength, and also suffering Han people's encroaching them.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years they had multiplied; grown fat and confident, they also smarted under every petty encroachment by Han settlers.

sentences.zh: 永初之元，騎都尉王弘使西域，發調羌、氏，以為行衛。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchu, Cavalry Commandant Wang Hong was sent to the Western Regions, issuing call-up of Qiang and Di, to serve as traveling guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongchu era, when Cavalry Commandant Wang Hong was dispatched to the Western Regions, the court levied Qiang and Di auxiliaries to escort him.

sentences.zh: 於是群羌奔駭，互相扇動，二州之戎，一時俱發，覆沒將守，屠破城邑。

translations.literal: Thereupon the mass Qiang ran in alarm, mutually fanning and moving; the Rong of the two provinces, at one time all rose, overturning and drowning generals and guards, slaughtering and breaking cities and towns.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang bands panicked, fanned one another into revolt, and the tribal forces of two provinces rose at once: they annihilated garrisons and magistrates and stormed walled towns.

sentences.zh: 鄧騭之征，棄甲委兵，輿屍喪師，前後相繼，諸戎遂熾，至於南入蜀漢，東掠趙、魏，唐突軹關，侵及河內。

translations.literal: In Deng Zhi's expedition, casting aside armor, abandoning weapons, carrying corpses, losing the army, one after another before and after, the various Rong thereupon blazed, reaching to south entering Shu and Han, east plundering Zhao and Wei, rudely bursting through Zhiguan, encroaching as far as Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Zhi's campaign ended in rout—armor thrown away, weapons abandoned, dead carried off in wagons, the army broken time and again—whereupon the tribes flared out of control, drove south into Shu and Han, raided east through Zhao and Wei, smashed past Zhiguan, and struck deep into Henei.

sentences.zh: 及遣北軍中候硃寵將五營士于孟津距羌，十年之中，夷夏俱斃，任尚、馬賢僅乃克之。

translations.literal: When they sent Northern Army Central Inspector Zhu Chong to lead Five Camp soldiers at Mengjin to resist the Qiang, within ten years, Yi and Xia both perished; Ren Shang and Ma Xian only then were able to overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Chong of the Northern Army was sent with the Five Garrisons to hold the Qiang at Mengjin, a decade of fighting bled barbarian and Chinese alike dry before Ren Shang and Ma Xian finally broke the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 此所以為害深重、累年不定者，雖由禦者之無方，將非其才，亦豈不以寇發心腹，害起肘腋，疢篤難療，瘡大遲愈之故哉！

translations.literal: This is the reason it became harm deep and heavy, years accumulated and not settled: although it was because the defenders lacked method, the generals were not their talents, was it not also because bandits issued from the heart and belly, harm arose from elbow and armpit, deep sickness hard to heal, great sores slow to heal?
translations.idiomatic: The revolt cut so deep and dragged on so long not only because command was inept and the wrong men were given armies, but because the enemy had risen in the empire's vitals—disaster in one's own elbow and armpit is a grave illness slow to cure and a wide wound long in closing.

sentences.zh: 自此之後，餘燼不盡，小有際會，輒復侵叛。

translations.literal: From this after, remaining embers not exhausted, slightly there being a juncture, then again encroached and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: After that the embers never died; the slightest opening brought fresh raids and defections.

sentences.zh: 馬賢忸忲，終於覆敗；

translations.literal: Ma Xian was hesitant and timid, finally ending in overturning defeat;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xian hesitated until his command collapsed in disaster;

sentences.zh: 段穎臨沖，自西徂樂。

translations.literal: Duan Ying faced the assault, from west proceeding to Le.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Jiong took the offensive and campaigned from the western frontier deep into the heartland.

sentences.zh: 雍州之戎，常為國患，中世之寇，惟此為大。

translations.literal: The Rong of Yongzhou constantly were the state's trouble; in mid-generation's bandits, only this was great.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes of Yongzhou were a standing national affliction; among the mid-Han invasions none matched this one in scale.

sentences.zh: 漢末之亂，關中殘滅。

translations.literal: In the disorder of Han's end, within the passes was remnant-destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The chaos at the end of the Han left Guanzhong a wasteland.

sentences.zh: 魏興之初，與蜀分隔，疆埸之戎，一彼一此。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wei's rise, with Shu separated, the Rong of the border fields, now that one now this one.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wei dynasty, with Shu Han cut off to the south, the tribal peoples along the contested frontier shifted back and forth with every campaign.

sentences.zh: 魏武皇帝令將軍夏侯妙才討叛氏阿貴、千萬等，後因拔棄漢中，遂徙武都之種于秦川，欲以弱寇強國，扞禦蜀虜。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei ordered General Xiahou Miaocai to punish the rebel Di Agui, Qianwan, and others; afterward because of pulling up and abandoning Hanzhong, thereupon moved the kinds of Wudu to the Qin plain, desiring thereby to weaken the bandit and strengthen the state, defending against the Shu captives.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent Xiahou Yuan against the rebel Di leaders Agui and Qianwan; later, when Wei abandoned Hanzhong, he resettled the Wudu Di on the Guanzhong plain, hoping to weaken the enemy, strengthen the state, and block Shu.

sentences.zh: 此蓋權宜之計，一時之勢，非所以為萬世之利也。

translations.literal: This was probably a expedient plan, one moment's circumstance, not that whereby to be ten thousand generations' profit.
translations.idiomatic: That was an expedient for the moment, not a policy that could secure lasting good.

sentences.zh: 今者當之，已受其弊矣。」

translations.literal: Now those who face it have already received its harm."
translations.idiomatic: We live with the consequences of that decision today, and we already feel the harm."

sentences.zh: 夫關中土沃物豐，厥田上上，加以涇、渭之流溉其舄鹵，鄭國、白渠灌浸相通，黍稷之饒，畝號一鐘，百姓謠詠其殷實，帝王之都每以為居，未聞戎狄宜在此土也。

translations.literal: Now within the passes the soil is fertile and things abundant, its fields upper-upper; moreover with the Jing and Wei streams irrigating its saline-alkali, the Zheng and Bai canals irrigation soaking mutually connected, the abundance of millet and panicled millet, mu called one zhong, the hundred songs and chant its fullness, the emperors' and kings' capitals each took this as dwelling; one has not heard that the Rong and Di are suitable on this soil.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong is rich soil in a top-grade belt: the Jing and Wei flush the salts from the fields, the Zheng and Bai canals weave irrigation across the plain, millet stands so thick that a single mu was said to yield a full zhong, and ballads celebrate its plenty. That is why dynasties make it their seat—never because barbarian herds belong there.

sentences.zh: 非我族類，其心必異，戎狄志態，不與華同。

translations.literal: Not our clan kind; their hearts must be different; the Rong and Di's aims and bearing are not the same as Hua.
translations.idiomatic: They are not of our kin, and their hearts cannot be the same; the aims and temper of the Rong and Di are not those of the Chinese.

sentences.zh: 而因其衰弊，遷之畿服，士庶玩習，侮其輕弱，使其怨恨之氣毒於骨髓。

translations.literal: Yet because of their decline and exhaustion, moving them to the capital domains, gentlemen and commoners play and practice, insulting their lightness and weakness, causing their resentful hatred qi to poison to the marrow.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in their weakness we have moved them into the capital region, where gentry and commoners, grown used to them, treat them with contempt because they seem powerless—until resentment lodges like poison in the bone.

sentences.zh: 至於蕃育眾盛，則坐生其心。

translations.literal: Reaching to multiplying and breeding, masses flourishing, then sitting they give birth to their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When they have multiplied and grown strong, rebellious intent springs up of itself.

sentences.zh: 以貪悍之性，挾憤怒之情，候隙乘便，輒為橫逆。

translations.literal: By greedy fierce nature, embracing angry rage feeling, waiting for crack, riding convenience, then acting as violence and perversity.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and fierce by nature, nursing rage, they watch for any opening and turn at once to violence.

sentences.zh: 而居封域之內，無障塞之隔，掩不備之人，收散野之積，故能為禍滋擾，暴害不測。

translations.literal: Yet dwelling within the enfeoffed domain's inside, without barrier passes' separation, masking unprepared people, gathering scattered wild's accumulations, therefore able to make disaster increase disturbance, violent harm not fathomable.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the Chinese heartland, with no mountain barriers between them and us, they can fall on an unwary populace and seize grain stored in the open; hence their ravages spread unpredictably.

sentences.zh: 此必然之勢，已驗之事也。

translations.literal: This is inevitable tendency, already verified matters.
translations.idiomatic: That is the logic of the situation, and history has already proved it.

sentences.zh: 當今之宜，宜及兵威方盛，眾事未罷，徙馮翊、北地、新平、安定界內諸羌，著先零、罕並、析支之地；

translations.literal: The fitness of the present day: it is fit while military might is just flourishing, the mass of affairs not yet ceased, to move the various Qiang within the borders of Fengyi, Beidi, Xinping, and Anding, settling them in the lands of Xianling, Hanbing, and Xizhi;
translations.idiomatic: The proper course now is, while our armies are still strong and before other tasks swallow our attention, to move every Qiang community inside Fengyi, Beidi, Xinping, and Anding back onto the traditional Xianling, Hanbing, and Xizhi ranges west of the frontier;

sentences.zh: 徙扶風、始平、京兆之氐，出還隴右，著陰平、武都之界。

translations.literal: move the Di of Fufeng, Shiping, and Jingzhao, out returning to Longyou's right, settling in the borders of Yinping and Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: to send the Di of Fufeng, Shiping, and Jingzhao out to Longyou again, settling them along the Yinping and Wudu frontier;

sentences.zh: 廩其道路之糧，令足自致，各附本種，反其舊土，使屬國、撫夷就安集之。

translations.literal: Granary their road's grain, order sufficient to self-arrive, each attach to original kind, return their old soil, causing dependent states, soothing Yi to approach and peacefully gather them.
translations.idiomatic: issue them grain for the march so they can reach home under their own power, let each band rejoin its own stock and return to its ancestral ground, and charge the dependent-state and frontier offices with settling them there.

sentences.zh: 戎晉不雜，並得其所，上合往古即敘之義，下為盛世永久之規。

translations.literal: Rong and Jin not mixed, both obtain their places; above joining the meaning of antiquity's immediate ordering, below being a prosperous age's permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and Chinese would no longer be intermingled; each would keep its proper place—honoring the ancient principle that barbarians who submit should be ordered without mixing, and giving the present age a lasting statute.

sentences.zh: 縱有猾夏之心，風塵之警，則絕遠中國，隔閡山河，雖為寇暴，所害不廣。

translations.literal: Even if there is cunning toward Xia heart, wind-dust alarms, then cut off far from the Middle Kingdom, blocked apart by mountains and rivers, although they act as bandit violence, the harm suffered is not broad.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they harbor designs on the Chinese heartland or raise dust on the frontier, they would be far from the interior, blocked by ranges and rivers; raids could not reach deep.

sentences.zh: 是以充國、子明能以數萬之眾制群羌之命，有征無戰，全軍獨克，雖有謀謨深計，廟勝遠圖，豈不以華夷異處，戎夏區別，要塞易守之故，得成其功也哉！

translations.literal: Therefore Chongguo and Ziming were able by several wan's multitude to control the mass Qiang's fate, having expeditions without battle, whole army alone conquering; although there were planning schemes deep plans, temple victory distant diagrams, was it not because Hua and Yi dwelt apart, Rong and Xia distinguished, strategic passes easy to defend's reason, obtaining completion of their merit?
translations.idiomatic: That is how Zhao Chongguo and Deng Ziming broke the Qiang hosts with a few ten thousand men, winning without full-scale battle and bringing the army home intact—less a miracle of strategy than the simple fact that Chinese and barbarian were separated, Rong and Xia kept apart, and the passes were easy to defend.

sentences.zh: 難者曰：方今關中之禍，暴兵二載，征戍之勞，老師十萬，水旱之害，薦饑累荒，疫癘之災，劄瘥夭昏。

translations.literal: The objector said: Just now the disaster within the passes, sudden soldiers two years, expedition garrison's toil, old army hundred thousand, flood and drought's harm, repeated famine piled desolation, pestilence's disaster, sudden death early darkening.
translations.idiomatic: An objector said: "Guanzhong has just endured two years of war, a hundred thousand troops worn out on campaign, flood and drought in succession, famine upon famine, plague cutting people down in their prime.

sentences.zh: 凶逆既戮，悔惡初附，且款且畏，咸懷危懼，百姓愁苦，異人同慮，望寧息之有期，若枯旱之思雨露，誠宜鎮之以安豫。

translations.literal: The fierce rebels already executed, those repenting evil first attached, both ingratiating and fearing, all cherishing danger and fear, the hundred surnames sorrowful and bitter, different people same anxiety, hoping for quiet rest's having a term, like drought's thinking of rain dew; truly it is fit to calm them with peace and ease.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels are dead; the newly submitted still waver between truce and terror; officials and commoners alike are exhausted and long for respite as parched earth longs for rain. Surely this is the time to soothe them, not stir them up."

sentences.zh: 而子方欲作役起徒，興功造事，使疲悴之眾，徙自猜之寇，以無穀之人，遷乏食之虜，恐勢盡力屈，緒業不卒，羌戎離散，心不可一，前害未及弭，而後變復橫出矣。

translations.literal: Yet you just desire to raise labor, start convicts, raise achievements, make affairs, causing weary and haggard masses, moving self-suspicious bandits, by grain-less people, relocating food-lacking captives; I fear power exhausted strength bent, thread work not completed, Qiang Rong scattered apart, hearts not able to be one, before harm not yet reached to extinguish, while after changes again horizontally emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you would press corvée on a broken people, march tribes who already distrust us, drive the hungry to move the starving—risking total exhaustion so the work never finishes, driving Qiang and Rong apart so they cannot be controlled together, leaving the old wounds open while fresh disasters break out."

sentences.zh: 答曰：羌戎狡猾，擅相號署，攻城野戰，傷害牧守，連兵聚眾，載離寒暑矣。

translations.literal: Answer said: The Qiang Rong are crafty and deceitful, presumptuously mutually proclaiming titles, attacking cities field battling, harming and injuring shepherds and guards, linking weapons gathering masses, years parting cold and heat.
translations.idiomatic: The reply ran: "The Qiang and Rong are cunning: they set up their own titles, storm towns and fight in the open, murder governors and commanders, and keep large hosts in the field year after year.

sentences.zh: 而今異類瓦解，同種土崩，老幼系虜，丁壯降散，禽離獸迸，不能相一。

translations.literal: But now different kinds tile-collapse, same kind earth-collapse, old and young tied captive, adult males surrender scattered, birds part beasts burst, not able mutually to be one.
translations.idiomatic: Now their alliance has shattered like tiles; each tribe is crumbling on its own; the old and young are bound captives, the fighting men scattered or surrendered; they bolt like startled beasts and cannot act as one.

sentences.zh: 子以此等為尚挾餘資，悔惡反善，懷我德惠而來柔附乎？

translations.literal: You take these sorts as still clutching surplus resources, repenting evil returning to good, cherishing our virtue and grace and coming soft attachment?
translations.idiomatic: Do you imagine they still hold hidden strength, that they repent and wish to return good for our kindness and come meekly to heel?

sentences.zh: 將勢窮道盡，智力俱困，懼我兵誅以至於此乎？

translations.literal: Or is it power exhausted way ended, wit and strength both trapped, fearing our weapons' punishment so as to reach to this?
translations.idiomatic: Or are they simply at the end of their rope, wit and strength spent, terrified of the sword and driven to this pass?

sentences.zh: 曰，無有餘力，勢窮道盡故也。

translations.literal: It is said: there is no surplus strength, power exhausted way ended's reason.
translations.idiomatic: The answer: they have no reserve left; they are cornered.

sentences.zh: 然則我能制其短長之命，而令其進退由己矣。

translations.literal: Then thus we are able to control their short and long fate, and order their advance and retreat to follow self.
translations.idiomatic: Then we hold their lives in our hands and may order their movements as we choose.

sentences.zh: 夫樂其業者不易事，安其居者無遷志。

translations.literal: Now those who delight in their work do not change affairs; those who peace their dwelling have no relocation will.
translations.idiomatic: Men who are happy in their trade do not welcome upheaval; men who are secure in their homes do not wish to move.

sentences.zh: 方其自疑危懼，畏怖促遽，故可制以兵威，使之左右無違也。

translations.literal: Just when they self-doubt danger and fear, fear and terror hurried and pressed, therefore can be controlled by military might, causing them left and right without disobedience.
translations.idiomatic: While they still doubt and dread us, we can overawe them with force and they will not dare refuse.

sentences.zh: 迨其死亡散流，離逷未鳩，與關中之人，戶皆為仇，故可遐遷遠處，令其心不懷土也。

translations.literal: When they die, scatter, flow, parted far not gathered, with within the passes people, every household all are enemies, therefore can be distantly moved far places, ordering their hearts not to cherish the soil.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when they are broken, scattered, not yet regrouped, and every household in Guanzhong counts them as enemies, we can march them far away so they will not cling to this soil.

sentences.zh: 夫聖賢之謀事也，為之於未有，理之於未亂，道不著而平，德不顯而成。

translations.literal: Now when sages and worthies plan affairs, they act them in not yet having, order them in not yet chaos, the Way not manifest yet level, virtue not displayed yet accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: The sage acts before crisis shows, orders things before riot breaks out, and brings peace without fanfare and success without ostentation.

sentences.zh: 其次則能轉禍為福，因敗為功，值困必濟，遇否能通。

translations.literal: Next then able to turn misfortune into fortune, borrow defeat for achievement, meeting distress necessarily ford, meeting obstruction able to penetrate.
translations.idiomatic: Next best is to turn danger into gain, snatch victory from defeat, find a ford in every strait, and pass through every block.

sentences.zh: 今子遭弊事之終而不圖更制之始，愛易轍之勤而得覆車之軌，何哉？

translations.literal: Now you meet exhausted affair's end yet do not plan more system's beginning, loving change rut's toil yet obtaining overturned cart's track—how?
translations.idiomatic: You would face the wreckage of a failed policy yet refuse to chart a new course—you shrink from the labor of changing course only to follow the cart into the same ditch. How is that wisdom?"

sentences.zh: 且關中之人百餘萬口，率其少多，戎狄居半，處之與遷，必須口實。

translations.literal: Moreover within the passes people exceed a million mouths; reckoning their fewer and more, the Rong and Di dwell half; settling them and moving them must have mouth food.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Guanzhong holds more than a million souls, and barbarians may be half of them; whether we keep them or move them, they must be fed.

sentences.zh: 若有窮乏糝粒不繼者，故當傾關中之谷以全其生生之計，必無擠於溝壑而不為侵掠之害也。

translations.literal: If there are exhausted poor grain not continuing ones, therefore ought to pour out within the passes grain to complete their living-living plan; assuredly none will be squeezed into ditches and gullies and not act as encroaching plunder's harm.
translations.idiomatic: If any lack even a handful of grain, we should empty the Guanzhong granaries to keep them alive; that way none are driven into the ditches to turn bandit and prey on others.

sentences.zh: 今我遷之，傳食而至，附其種族，自使相贍，而秦地之人得其半穀，此為濟行者以廩糧，遺居者以積倉，寬關中之逼，去盜賊之原，除旦夕之損，建終年之益。

translations.literal: Now we move them, relay food and arrive, attach to their clans and kinds, self causing mutual provision, while Qin land's people obtain their half grain; this is to ford travelers by granary grain, leave dwellers by piled granaries, widen within the presses' pressure, remove bandit-thieves' source, eliminate dawn and dusk's harm, establish full year's profit.
translations.idiomatic: Move them now: issue rations along the road, let each join its own kin so they feed one another, and the Chinese of Qin will keep half the grain they would have lost—feeding the marchers, leaving stores for those who stay, easing the crush in Guanzhong, cutting off the root of banditry, lifting today's crisis, and securing peace for years to come.

sentences.zh: 若憚暫舉之小勞，而忘永逸之弘策；

translations.literal: If one fears temporary undertaking's small toil, yet forgets forever ease's great strategy;
translations.idiomatic: To shrink from the brief pain of the move and forget the grand policy that buys lasting peace—

sentences.zh: 惜日月之煩苦，而遺累世之寇敵，非所謂能開物成務，創業垂統，崇其拓跡，謀及子孫者也。

translations.literal: cherish sun and moon's vexation and bitterness, yet leave piled generations' bandit foes—not that called able to open things complete tasks, found enterprise hang thread, exalt their expanded traces, plan reaching to sons and grandsons ones.
translations.idiomatic: to spare a few months of trouble and bequeath an enemy to posterity is not what is meant by mastering affairs, founding a line that will last, widening the realm's footprint, or planning for one's children and grandchildren."

sentences.zh: 并州之胡，本實匈奴桀惡之寇也。

translations.literal: The Hu of Bingzhou, fundamentally are really Xiongnu fierce evil bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu of Bingzhou are, at root, the fierce core of the Xiongnu horsemen.

sentences.zh: 漢宣之世，凍餒殘破，國內五裂，後合為二，呼韓邪遂衰弱孤危，不能自存，依阻塞下，委質柔服。

translations.literal: In the time of Han's Xuandi, frozen and starved remnant-broken, within the state five split, afterward combined as two, Huhanye then weak alone perilous, unable self to preserve, relying on barrier block below, entrusted substance soft submission.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan of Han they were broken by cold and hunger and split into five hordes that later merged into two; Huhanye grew so weak he could not survive alone, clung to the frontier passes, and offered submission.

sentences.zh: 建武中，南單于復來降附，遂令入塞，居於漠南，數世之後，亦輒叛戾，故何熙、梁槿戎車屢征。

translations.literal: In Jianwu, the Southern Chanyu again came surrendering attaching, thereupon ordered to enter the passes, dwelling south of the desert; after several generations, also then rebelled perverse; therefore He Xi and Liang Jin war chariots repeatedly campaigned.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianwu era the Southern Shanyu submitted again and was allowed inside the line to live south of the desert; within a few generations he was in revolt again, which is why He Xi and Liang Jin had to campaign so often.

sentences.zh: 中平中，以黃巾賊起，發調其兵，部眾不從，而殺羌渠。

translations.literal: In Zhongping, because Yellow Turban bandits arose, issued call-up their troops; the division masses did not obey, and killed Qiang Qu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhongping era, when the Yellow Turbans rose, the court called out the Southern Xiongnu host; they refused the order and murdered their own chief, the Qiangqu.

sentences.zh: 由是於彌扶羅求助於漢，以討其賊。

translations.literal: From this Yu Mifuluo sought help from Han, in order to punish their bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yufuluo thereupon begged Han aid against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 仍值世喪亂，遂乘釁而作，鹵掠趙、魏，寇至河南。

translations.literal: Still meeting generation loss chaos, thereupon riding crack and acting, capturing and plundering Zhao and Wei, bandits reaching south of the River.
translations.idiomatic: The realm then fell into chaos; he seized the moment, raided Zhao and Wei, and struck south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 建安中，又使右賢王去卑誘質呼廚泉，聽其部落散居六郡。

translations.literal: In Jian'an, again ordered Right Worthy King Qubi to entice and hold hostage Huchuquan, listening to their tribes scattered dwelling in six commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jian'an years the court had the Right Worthy King Quibi detain Shanyu Huchuquan and allowed the tribes to scatter across six commanderies.

sentences.zh: 咸熙之際，以一部太強，分為三率。

translations.literal: At the Xianxi juncture, because one division too strong, divided into three commands.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wei, because one division had grown too strong, it was split into three commands.

sentences.zh: 泰始之初，又增為四。

translations.literal: At Taishi's beginning, again increased to four.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taishi era the court raised that number to four.

sentences.zh: 於是劉猛內叛，連結外虜。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liu Meng inside rebelled, linking connecting outer captives.
translations.idiomatic: Then Liu Meng rebelled inside the border and allied with tribes beyond.

sentences.zh: 近者郝散之變，發于穀遠。

translations.literal: Near, Hao San's change, issued from Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: More recently the mutiny of Hao San began in Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 今五部之眾，戶至數萬，人口之盛，過於西戎。

translations.literal: Now the five divisions' masses, households reaching several ten thousands, mouths' flourishing, exceeding the western Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Today the five divisions number their households in the tens of thousands; their population outnumbers the western tribes.

sentences.zh: 然其天性驍勇，弓馬便利，倍於氐、羌。

translations.literal: Yet their heaven-nature fierce brave, bow horse convenient sharp, doubled compared to Di and Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: They are fiercer by nature and doubly more adept with bow and horse than the Di or Qiang.

sentences.zh: 若有不虞風塵之慮，則并州之域可為寒心。

translations.literal: If there is unanticipated wind-dust worry, then Bingzhou's territory can be cold heart.
translations.idiomatic: If alarm should rise on the frontier, the whole Bingzhou region will shudder.

sentences.zh: 滎陽句驪本居遼東塞外，正始中，幽州刺史毋丘儉伐其叛者，徙其餘種。

translations.literal: The Xingyang Goguryeo originally dwelled beyond the passes in Liaodong; in the Zhengshi period, Inspector of Youzhou Guqiu Jian campaigned against their rebels and moved their remaining kinds.
translations.idiomatic: The Goguryeo clans settled at Xingyang had originally lived beyond the Liaodong frontier; during the Zhengshi era, Guqiu Jian, inspector of Youzhou, attacked their rebel bands and resettled the survivors inside China.

sentences.zh: 始徙之時，戶落百數，子孫孳息，今以千計，數世之後，必至殷熾。

translations.literal: At the time they first were moved, households fell in the hundreds; sons and grandsons multiplied; now they are reckoned by thousands; after several generations, they will surely reach fullness and blaze.
translations.idiomatic: At first there were only a few hundred households; generation on generation they have bred until they are counted in the thousands, and in a few more generations they will swell to enormous strength.

sentences.zh: 今百姓失職，猶或亡叛，犬馬肥充，則有噬齧，況于夷狄，能不為變！

translations.literal: Now the hundred surnames lose office, still some flee and rebel; dogs and horses fat and full, then there is biting and gnawing—how much more as to the Yi and Di, can they not become change!
translations.idiomatic: Chinese commoners who have lost their livelihoods still sometimes flee or rise in revolt; when dogs and horses grow fat they turn to bite—how much more will alien peoples seize the moment to rebel!

sentences.zh: 但顧其微弱勢力不陳耳。

translations.literal: Only they are regarded as weak and slight, their power and situation not displayed.
translations.idiomatic: We only imagine them too weak for their strength to show—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 夫為邦者，患不在貧而在不均，憂不在寡而在不安。

translations.literal: Now those who govern a state, their trouble lies not in poverty but in unevenness; their worry lies not in fewness but in not peace.
translations.idiomatic: He who governs a state should fear not poverty but inequality, not a small population but unrest.

sentences.zh: 以四海之廣，士庶之富，豈須夷虜在內，然後取足哉！

translations.literal: By the four seas' breadth, the abundance of gentlemen and commoners, how must barbarian captives be within, and only then obtain sufficiency!
translations.idiomatic: The realm is vast and our people numerous—do we really need barbarians living inside the border before we can prosper!

sentences.zh: 此等皆可申諭發遣，還其本域，慰彼羈旅懷土之思，釋我華夏纖介之憂。

translations.literal: These sorts all can be declared and instructed, issued and dispatched, returned to their original regions, comforting those sojourners' cherishing-soil thoughts, releasing our Hua-Xia's fine-hair's anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Every such group may be clearly ordered home to its own country, easing their homesickness as wanderers and lifting from the Chinese heartland even the slightest gnawing fear.

sentences.zh: 惠此中國，以綏四方，德施永世，于計為長。

translations.literal: Show favor to this Central Kingdom, thereby to pacify the four quarters; virtue extending through ages—in reckoning this is the long.
translations.idiomatic: Bless the Central Plains and the four quarters will settle; a policy whose virtue endures for generations is, all things weighed, the soundest course.

sentences.zh: 帝不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor could not use it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor declined to act on the proposal.

sentences.zh: 未及十年，而夷狄亂華，時服其深識。

translations.literal: Before reaching ten years, then the Yi and Di disordered Huaxia; people of the time submitted to his deep insight.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten years the barbarians had thrown the Chinese world into chaos, and contemporaries conceded how far-sighted he had been.

sentences.zh: 遷中郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Central Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to the rank of Central Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 選司以統叔父春為宜春令，統因上疏曰：「故事，父祖與官職同名，皆得改選，而未有身與官職同名，不在改選之例。

translations.literal: The selection bureau appointed Tong's paternal uncle Chun as magistrate of Yichun; Tong therefore submitted a memorial saying: "By precedent, when fathers or grandfathers share a name with an office title, all may obtain changed selection, but there has never been a case of one's own person sharing a name with an office title, not falling within the cases for changed selection.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Appointments named Tong's uncle Jiang Chun magistrate of Yichun, whereupon Tong submitted a memorial: "By established rule, when a father or grandfather shares a name with an official title, he may be reassigned to another post, yet no precedent addresses the case in which the official himself bears the same name as his title and is excluded from reassignment.

sentences.zh: 臣以為父祖改選者，蓋為臣子開地，不為父祖之身也。

translations.literal: Your subject believes that when fathers and grandfathers change selection, it is generally to open ground for sons and grandsons, not for fathers' and grandfathers' persons themselves.
translations.idiomatic: I believe reassignment when a father's or grandfather's name clashes with an office is meant to clear a path for his descendants, not chiefly to spare the elder himself.

sentences.zh: 而身名所加，亦施于臣子。

translations.literal: Yet what the personal name applies to also extends to sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: The burden of a taboo name falls on subordinates and heirs no less than on the man who holds the title.

sentences.zh: 佐吏系屬，朝夕從事，官位之號，發言所稱，若指實而語，則違經禮諱尊之義；

translations.literal: Assistant clerks are bound and attached, morning and evening pursuing affairs; the designation of office rank is what speech names—if pointing to the real and speaking, then it violates the classics and rites' meaning of tabooing the honored;
translations.idiomatic: Aides are tied to their chief day and night; they must speak his official title aloud—yet to name it plainly breaks the canonical rule of avoiding the superior's name;

sentences.zh: 若詭辭避回，則為廢官擅犯憲制。

translations.literal: if using deceitful phrases to evade and turn aside, then it is nullifying office and presumptuously violating the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: to dodge with circumlocution is to nullify the dignity of the office and breach the written law.

sentences.zh: 今以四海之廣，職位之眾，名號繁多，士人殷富，至使有受寵皇朝，出身宰牧，而令佐吏不得表其官稱，子孫不得言其位號，所以上嚴君父，下為臣子，體例不通。

translations.literal: Now by the four seas' breadth, the multitude of posts, names and titles abundant and numerous, scholars abundant and rich, reaching to the point that some receive favor at the imperial court, emerge as shepherds and magistrates, yet are ordered that assistant clerks may not display their official titles, sons and grandsons may not speak their rank titles—thereby above strictly honoring lord father, below acting for sons and grandsons, regulations do not connect.
translations.idiomatic: Today posts are countless and the gentry numerous; some who win honor at court and go out as governors find their clerks forbidden to utter their proper titles and their children forbidden to speak their ranks—so the ruler is honored above while the forms that bind lord and subject below are left incoherent.

sentences.zh: 若易私名以避官職，則違《春秋》不奪人親之義。

translations.literal: If changing private names to avoid office titles, then it violates the Spring and Autumn's meaning of not stripping others of their kin.
translations.idiomatic: To change one's personal name to dodge an office would violate the Spring and Autumn Annals' principle that one must not strip another of the name his kin gave him.

sentences.zh: 臣以為身名與官職同者，宜與觸父祖名為比，體例既全，於義為弘。

translations.literal: Your subject believes that cases where personal name matches office title ought to be classed with touching fathers' and grandfathers' names; the pattern being then complete, in righteousness it is ampler.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that when a man's own name matches his title, the case should be treated like the ordinary taboo on a parent's name: the rule is then complete and the moral logic clearer.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷從之。

translations.literal: " The court followed it.
translations.idiomatic: " The court accepted his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 轉太子洗馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred to heir-apparent's groom.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of groom for the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 在東宮累年，甚被親禮。

translations.literal: In the Eastern Palace many years, he was very received in intimate courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He served for years in the Eastern Palace and was treated with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 太子頗闕朝覲，又奢費過度，多諸禁忌，統上書諫曰：

translations.literal: The heir apparent was rather lacking in court audiences, and also was excessive in luxury and expense, with many sorts of taboos; Tong submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent often neglected his court duties, spent lavishly, and surrounded himself with superstitious taboos; Jiang Tong therefore addressed a memorial of remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 臣聞古之為臣者，進思盡忠，退思補過，獻可替否，拾遺補闕。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that those who were ministers in antiquity, advancing thought to exhaust loyalty, withdrawing thought to mend faults, presenting the acceptable and replacing the not, gathering oversights and mending gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers in antiquity strove in court to fulfill their loyalty, in retirement to mend their faults, offered what was sound and rejected what was not, and repaired every oversight in the ruler's conduct.

sentences.zh: 是以人主得以舉無失行，言無口過，德音發聞，揚名後世。

translations.literal: Thereby the human lord was able to act without losing conduct, speak without mouth faults, virtue's sound issuing and heard, raising name in later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the sovereign could act without misstep, speak without indiscretion, let his virtuous fame be heard abroad, and leave a shining name to posterity.

sentences.zh: 臣等不逮，無能雲補，思竭愚誠，謹陳五事如左，惟蒙一省再省，少垂察納。

translations.literal: Your subjects are not reaching, without ability to cloud-supplement; thinking to exhaust foolish sincerity, respectfully set forth five matters as at left; only hoping to receive one examination and again examination, slightly letting fall inspection and acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: We are unequal to such a standard and cannot mend every fault, yet we wish to offer our utmost loyalty and therefore respectfully lay out five points below, begging Your Highness to read them once and again and to deign to accept what is sound.

sentences.zh: 其一曰，六行之義，以孝為首，虞舜之德，以孝為稱，故太子以朝夕視君膳為職，左右就養無方。

translations.literal: The first says: the meaning of the six conducts takes filial piety as head; Shun of Yu's virtue took filial piety as its designation; therefore the heir apparent takes morning and evening inspecting the lord's meals as duty, left and right attending nurture without pattern.
translations.idiomatic: First: among the six virtues filial piety comes first, and Shun of Yu was praised above all for filial devotion; it is the crown prince's duty to attend his father's meals morning and evening and to care for him tirelessly on every side.

sentences.zh: 文王之為世子，可謂篤於事親者也，故能擅三代之美，為百王之宗。

translations.literal: King Wen's being heir can be called earnest in serving kin; therefore he was able to monopolize the three dynasties' beauty, be the hundred kings' ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen as crown prince showed the utmost devotion to his parents; hence he gathered up the finest virtue of the three dynasties and became the model for kings through the ages.

sentences.zh: 自頃聖體屢有疾患，數闕朝侍，遠近觀聽者不能深知其故，以致疑惑。

translations.literal: Since recently the sagely person has repeatedly had illness and ailment, often lacking court attendance; far and near observers and listeners cannot deeply know its reasons, thereby reaching doubt and confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Lately Your Majesty's health has often troubled you, so that court attendance has been irregular; those near and far who watch and listen do not know the true reasons and harbor doubts.

sentences.zh: 伏願殿下雖有微苦，可堪扶輿，則宜自力。

translations.literal: We bow wishing Your Highness, although having slight suffering, if able to bear being supported in the carriage, then ought to exert self.
translations.idiomatic: We pray that whenever Your Highness can endure the carriage, however slight your discomfort, you will force yourself to attend.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「君子終日乾乾。

translations.literal: The Changes says: "The noble man all day qian-qian.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "The gentleman is wary all day long."

sentences.zh: 」蓋自勉強不息之謂也。

translations.literal: " This is what is called self-strengthening without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: " That is what is meant by ceaseless self-exertion."

sentences.zh: 其二曰，古之人君雖有聰明之姿，睿喆之質，必須輔弼之助，相導之功，故虞舜以五臣興，周文以四友隆。

translations.literal: The second says: ancient human lords although having clever-bright bearing, wise and wise substance, must have assist-support's help, mutual guidance's merit; therefore Shun of Yu by five ministers rose, Zhou Wen by four friends flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Second: even rulers gifted with native intelligence need tutors to guide them—Shun of Yu rose with the help of five ministers, King Wen of Zhou flourished with the four companions.

sentences.zh: 及成王之為太子也，則周、召為保傅，史佚昭文章，故能聞道早備，登崇大業，刑措不用，流聲洋溢。

translations.literal: When it reached King Cheng's being heir, then Zhou and Shao were protectors and tutors, Shi Yi displayed pattern and culture; therefore he was able to hear the Way early and prepare, ascend and exalt great enterprise, punishments set aside not used, flowing sound overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: When King Cheng was crown prince, the dukes of Zhou and Shao served as his guardians and tutors, and Shi Yi opened his eyes to letters; thus he learned the Way while young, mounted the great enterprise, left the punishments unused, and his fame spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 伏惟殿下天授逸才，聰鑒特達，臣謂猶宜時發聖令，宣揚德音，諮詢保傅，訪逮侍臣，覲見賓客，得令接盡，壅否之情沛然交泰，殿下之美煥然光明。

translations.literal: We bow think Your Highness heaven-bestowed transcendent talent, clever mirror especially penetrating; your subjects say still it is fit from time to time to issue sagely commands, proclaim and raise virtue's sound, consult protectors and tutors, visit and reach attendant ministers, personally see guests, able to order reception to the utmost, blocked and not feelings abundantly intersecting peace, Your Highness's beauty blazingly bright.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness's talents are heaven-given and your discernment keen; we would still urge you to issue edicts from time to time, let your virtuous intentions be heard, question your tutors and attendants, receive guests face to face, and let every obstruction between ruler and served dissolve in openness—so your luster may shine the brighter.

sentences.zh: 如此，則高朗之風，扇於前人；

translations.literal: If thus, then the high and bright wind fans before others;
translations.idiomatic: Then your lofty openness will set a tone that reaches back to the finest examples of the past;

sentences.zh: 弘範令軌，永為後式。

translations.literal: great model and fine track, forever be later pattern.
translations.idiomatic: your magnanimity will set a lasting pattern for those who come after.

sentences.zh: 其三曰，古之聖王莫不以儉為德，故堯稱采椽茅茨，禹稱卑宮惡服，漢文身衣弋綈，足履革舄，以身先物，政致太平，存為明王，沒見宗祀。

translations.literal: The third says: ancient sage kings none did not take frugality as virtue; therefore Yao was called plucked rafters thatched huts, Yu was called low palace bad clothes, Han Wen personally clothed in black silk, feet treading leather slippers, with body taking the lead over things, government reaching great peace, alive was bright king, dead seen in ancestral sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Third: the sage kings of old all made frugality their chief virtue—Yao with his unplaned rafters and thatched hall, Yu with his low palace and coarse dress, Emperor Wen of Han in black homespun and leather shoes, putting himself before his people and bringing about great peace, honored in life and enshrined after death.

sentences.zh: 及諸侯修之者，魯僖以躬儉節用，聲列《雅頌》；

translations.literal: Reaching the feudal lords who cultivated it, Duke Xi of Lu by personally frugal economizing use, sound arrayed in Ya and Song;
translations.idiomatic: Among the feudal lords, Duke Xi of Lu won a place in the canonical Odes, in the Ya and Song sections, for personal thrift and careful spending;

sentences.zh: 蚡冒以篳路藍縷，用張楚國。

translations.literal: Fenmao by splintered chariot tattered cloth, thereby expanded Chu state.
translations.idiomatic: King Fenmao of Chu, riding a wicker cart in rags, laid the foundations of a powerful kingdom.

sentences.zh: 大夫修之者，文子相魯，妾不衣帛；

translations.literal: Among great officers who cultivated it, Wenzi was minister of Lu, concubines not clothed in silk;
translations.idiomatic: Among great officers, Wenzi as minister of Lu would not let his concubines wear silk;

sentences.zh: 晏嬰相齊，鹿裘不補，亦能匡君濟俗，興國隆家。

translations.literal: Yan Ying was minister of Qi, deer fur robe not mended; also was able to rectify the lord and aid custom, raise state and exalt house.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ying as minister of Qi wore an unmended deer-hide cloak, yet he could correct his ruler, improve the customs, and bring glory to state and clan.

sentences.zh: 庶人修之者，顏回以簞食瓢飲，揚其仁聲；

translations.literal: Among commoners who cultivated it, Yan Hui by basket food gourd drink, raised his benevolent sound;
translations.idiomatic: Among commoners, Yan Hui with his basket of grain and gourd of water made his humane reputation known;

sentences.zh: 原憲以蓬戶繩樞，邁其清德。

translations.literal: Yuan Xian by tumbleweed door rope pivot, exceeded in clear virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian in his gate of woven brush and hinge of cord surpassed others in purity of character.

sentences.zh: 此皆聖主明君賢臣智士之所履行也。

translations.literal: These all are what bright sage lords, wise ministers, and wise scholars practiced and walked.
translations.idiomatic: These are examples set by enlightened sovereigns, worthy ministers, and wise men.

sentences.zh: 故能懸名日月，永世不朽，蓋儉之福也。

translations.literal: Therefore able to hang name with sun and moon, eternal generations not rotten; this is frugality's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Their names hang beside the sun and moon and never fade—such is the blessing of frugality.

sentences.zh: 及到末世，以奢失之者，帝王則有瑤台瓊室，玉懷象箸，肴膳之珍則熊蹯豹胎，酒池肉林。

translations.literal: Reaching the final age, those who by luxury lost it, emperors and kings then had jade terraces and carnelian chambers, jade cups and ivory chopsticks, in delicacies of meats and dishes then bear paws and leopard fetuses, wine pools and meat forests.
translations.idiomatic: At a dynasty's end, those who lost all through extravagance built jade towers and carnelian halls, drank from jade cups with ivory chopsticks, feasted on bear paw and leopard fetus, and dug wine pools amid forests of hanging meat.

sentences.zh: 諸侯為之者，至於丹楹刻桷，餼征百牢。

translations.literal: Feudal lords who did it reached to vermilion pillars carved rafters, grain for expedition hundred pens.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal lords painted their pillars red and carved their eaves, and sent a hundred oxen as fodder for a single army march.

sentences.zh: 大夫有瓊弁玉纓，庶人有擊鐘鼎食。

translations.literal: Great officers had carnelian cap tassels of jade; commoners had striking bells and tripod eating.
translations.idiomatic: Great officers wore jade tassels on carnelian caps; commoners tolled bells and ate from tripods as if they were nobles.

sentences.zh: 亦罔不亡國喪宗，破家失身，醜名彰聞，以為後戒。

translations.literal: Also none did not lose state and destroy lineage, break house and lose body, ugly name displayed and heard, to be later warning.
translations.idiomatic: Not one failed to lose his state, destroy his line, ruin his house, and die in infamy—a warning to later ages.

sentences.zh: 竊聞後園鏤飾金銀，刻磨犀象，畫室之巧，課試日精。

translations.literal: We have heard that the rear garden carves and ornaments gold and silver, engraves and polishes rhinoceros and ivory, the painting chamber's skill, examined and tested daily refined.
translations.idiomatic: We hear that the rear garden is inlaid with gold and silver, that rhinoceros horn and ivory are carved and polished, and that painters compete daily in ever finer craft.

sentences.zh: 臣等以為今四海之廣，萬物之富，以今方古，不足為侈也。

translations.literal: Your subjects think that now the four seas' breadth, the myriad things' wealth, comparing present to antiquity, is not sufficient to be extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: We grant that the realm is wide and goods abundant, and by comparison with antiquity your splendor might still seem modest.

sentences.zh: 然上之所好，下必從之，是故居上者必慎其所好也。

translations.literal: Yet what those above delight in, those below must follow; therefore those who dwell above must be careful in what they delight in.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people always imitate what their betters love; a ruler must therefore be wary of his tastes.

sentences.zh: 昔漢光武皇帝時，有獻千里馬及寶劍者，馬以駕鼓車，劍以賜騎士。

translations.literal: Formerly in Han Emperor Guangwu's time, there were those who presented a thousand-li horse and a precious sword; the horse was used to pull the drum cart, the sword was given to a mounted knight.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangwu of Han received a thousand-li horse and a treasured sword, he hitched the horse to a baggage cart and gave the sword to a common trooper.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝有上雉頭裘者，即詔有司焚之都街。

translations.literal: Shizu Emperor Wu had one who presented a pheasant-head fur robe; immediately ordered the responsible officials to burn it in the capital street.
translations.idiomatic: When someone offered Emperor Wu a cloak sewn from pheasant heads, he ordered it burned at once in the public street.

sentences.zh: 高世之主，不尚尤物，故能正天下之俗，刑四方之風。

translations.literal: High-generation lords do not esteem extraordinary things; therefore able to rectify all under Heaven's customs, model the four quarters' winds.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers who tower above their age do not hoard curiosities; thus they set the empire's customs aright and give the four quarters a model to follow.

sentences.zh: 臣等以為畫室之功，可且減省，後園雜作，一皆罷遣，肅然清靜，優遊道德，則日新之美光于四海矣。

translations.literal: Your subjects think that the painting chamber's work may for the nonce be reduced and cut; rear garden miscellaneous works, all together dismiss and send away; solemnly pure and quiet, leisurely roam in virtue and power, then daily renewal's beauty will shine on the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that work on the painting galleries be curtailed for now, every superfluous project in the rear gardens stopped, and the palace kept solemn and still so that Your Highness may cultivate the Way in leisure—then the glory of daily renewal will reach the four seas.

sentences.zh: 其四曰，以天下而供一人，以百里而供諸侯，故王侯食藉而衣稅，公卿大夫受爵而資祿，莫有不贍者也。

translations.literal: The fourth says: by all under Heaven to supply one person, by hundred li to supply the feudal lords; therefore kings and marquises eat rent and clothe from tax, dukes and ministers and great officers receive rank and rely on salary—none without sufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: the whole realm feeds the ruler and each hundred li feeds its lord; kings and marquises live on rent and tax, ministers on stipends tied to rank—none should want for enough.

sentences.zh: 是以士農工商四業不雜。

translations.literal: Therefore scholar, farmer, artisan, merchant four occupations not mixed.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the four orders—scholar, farmer, artisan, and merchant—were kept distinct.

sentences.zh: 交易而退，以通有無者，庶人之業也。

translations.literal: Exchanging and trading then withdrawing, thereby to connect having and not having—this is the commoners' occupation.
translations.idiomatic: To exchange goods and retire, supplying mutual wants, was the commoner's trade.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》三市，旦則百族，晝則商賈，夕則販夫販婦。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou three markets: dawn then hundred clans, day then merchants, evening then peddling husbands and peddling wives.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou speaks of three markets: at dawn the common clans trade, by day the merchants, at dusk the hawking men and women.

sentences.zh: 買賤賣貴，販鬻菜果，收十百之盈，以救旦夕之命，故為庶人之貧賤者也。

translations.literal: Buying cheap selling dear, vending vegetables and fruits, gathering ten and hundred's surplus, thereby to save dawn and dusk's life—therefore they are the commoners' poor and base.
translations.idiomatic: They buy cheap and sell dear, peddle greens and fruit, and eke out a few cash to keep body and soul together—hence they rank as the humble sort.

sentences.zh: 樊遲匹夫，請學為圃，仲尼不答；

translations.literal: Fan Chi the common fellow, requested to study being gardener; Zhongni did not answer;
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Chi, a mere commoner, asked to learn gardening, Confucius gave no answer;

sentences.zh: 魯大夫臧文仲使妾織蒲，又譏其不仁；

translations.literal: Lu great officer Zang Wenzhong caused concubines to weave rushes, and was again ridiculed as not benevolent;
translations.idiomatic: Zang Wenzhong of Lu had his concubines weave rush mats for sale and was judged harshly for it;

sentences.zh: 公儀子相魯，則拔其園葵，言食祿者不與貧賤之人爭利也。

translations.literal: Gongyi Xiu was minister of Lu, then pulled up his garden mallow, saying those who eat salary do not with poor base persons contend profit.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi Xiu as minister of Lu tore up the mallows in his garden, declaring that an official who draws a stipend must not compete with the poor for petty gain.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢以來，風俗轉薄，公侯之尊，莫不殖園圃之田，而收市井之利，漸冉相放，莫以為恥，乘以古道，誠可愧也。

translations.literal: Since Qin and Han, customs turned thin; the honor of dukes and marquises, none did not propagate garden and orchard fields, and collect market and well's profit, gradually imitating one another, none taking it as shame; measured by ancient ways, truly shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qin and Han, morals have thinned until even the highest nobles plant market gardens and squeeze profit from the bazaar, each copying the next without shame—set against the ancient norm it is a disgrace.

sentences.zh: 今西園賣葵菜、藍子、雞、面之屬，虧敗國體，貶損令問。

translations.literal: Now the Western Garden sells mallow greens, indigo seeds, chicken, noodles and the like, injuring and defeating the state's body, diminishing and harming fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: To peddle greens, indigo seed, chickens, and noodles from the Western Park injures the dignity of the state and blackens your good name.

sentences.zh: 其五曰，竊見禁土，令不得繕修牆壁，動正屋瓦。

translations.literal: The fifth says: we have seen forbidden ground, orders not permitting repairing walls, moving main house tiles.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: we note that tabooed ground has been declared off limits so that none may mend walls or replace tiles on principal roofs.

sentences.zh: 臣以為此既違典彝舊義，且以拘攣小忌而廢弘廓大道，宜可蠲除，於事為宜。

translations.literal: Your subjects think this already violates canonical vessels' old meaning, and moreover by cramped small taboos abandons great and vast great Way; it is fit to be remitted and removed—in affairs this is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: This runs against classical precedent and lets petty superstition block the broad highway of government; it should be abolished as the right course.

sentences.zh: 朝廷善之。

translations.literal: The court deemed it good.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his advice.

sentences.zh: 後為博士、尚書郎，參大司馬、齊王冏軍事。

translations.literal: Afterward he was erudite, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, participated in Grand Marshal Prince of Qi Jiong's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as an academician, a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and staff adviser on military affairs to Sima Jiong, the Prince of Qi and grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 冏驕荒將敗，統切諫，文多不載。

translations.literal: Jiong was arrogant and wasteful and about to be defeated; Tong remonstrated keenly; the text much is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong grew arrogant and dissolute on the eve of his ruin; Jiang Tong remonstrated bluntly—the memorials were many and are not preserved here.

sentences.zh: 遷廷尉正，每州郡疑獄，斷處從輕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of Justice rectifier; whenever prefectures and commanderies had doubtful cases, in deciding he followed the light.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to senior rectifier in the ministry of justice and, whenever a commandery sent up a doubtful case, always resolved it leniently.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎請為記室，多所箴諫。

translations.literal: Prince of Chengdu Ying requested him as secretary; he had many admonitions and remonstrances.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying of Chengdu appointed him secretary and received many frank admonitions from him.

sentences.zh: 申論陸雲兄弟，辭甚切至。

translations.literal: He extended argument for Lu Yun and his brothers; the wording was very keen and utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke out forcefully on behalf of Lu Yun and his brother, and his language was urgent in the extreme.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Because of mother's mourning he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為司徒左長史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he became Minister of Education left senior clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, he was appointed senior clerk on the left of the minister of education.

sentences.zh: 東海王越為兗州牧，以統為別駕，委以州事，與統書曰：「昔王子師為豫州，未下車，辟荀慈明；

translations.literal: Prince of the Eastern Sea Yue was Yanzhou shepherd, taking Tong as aide-de-camp, entrusted him with prefecture affairs, and wrote to Tong saying: "Formerly Wang Zishi was Yu prefect; before descending the cart, he summoned Xun Ciming;
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yue, Prince of the Eastern Sea, became governor of Yanzhou, he named Jiang Tong his aide-de-camp and entrusted him with the administration of the province, writing to him: "In old days Wang Yun, as governor of Yu Province, before his carriage even halted, appointed Xun Cai to office;

sentences.zh: 下車，辟孔文舉。

translations.literal: after descending the cart, summoned Kong Wenju.
translations.idiomatic: after it halted, he appointed Kong Rong."

sentences.zh: 貴州人士有堪應此者不？

translations.literal: Are there among your noble prefecture's gentlemen persons able to answer this?
translations.idiomatic: Are there men in your province fit to answer that precedent?"

sentences.zh: 」統舉高平郗鑒為賢良，陳留阮修為直言，濟北程收為方正，時以為知人。

translations.literal: " Tong raised Gaoping Xi Jian as worthy and good, Chenliu Ruan Xiu as outspoken straight, Jibei Cheng Shou as upright and square; people of the time thought him knowing of men.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiang Tong recommended Xi Jian of Gaoping as worthy and excellent, Ruan Xiu of Chenliu as candid critic, and Cheng Shou of Jibei as upright and incorrupt; contemporaries praised his eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 尋遷黃門侍郎、散騎常侍，領國子博士。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Yellow Gate Gentleman, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently director of the imperial academy.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was promoted to gentleman at the yellow gates, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and concurrent erudite of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 永嘉四年，避難奔于成皋，病卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongjia, fleeing disaster he ran to Chenggao, and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongjia he fled the turmoil to Chenggao, where he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 凡所造賦頌表奏皆傳於後。

translations.literal: All that he composed in rhapsodies, odes, memorials, and petitions was transmitted to later.
translations.idiomatic: The rhapsodies, eulogies, memorials, and petitions he wrote have all come down to later times.

sentences.zh: 二子：虨、惇。

translations.literal: Two sons: Bin and Dun.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Jiang Bin and Jiang Dun.

sentences.zh: 虨字思玄，本州辟舉秀才，平南將軍溫嶠以為參軍。

translations.literal: Bin, courtesy name Sixuan, the prefecture summoned and raised him as cultivated talent; General Who Pacifies the South Wen Qiao took him as army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bin, courtesy name Sixuan, was nominated as a cultivated talent by his home province and taken on as an army adviser by Wen Qiao, general who pacifies the south.

sentences.zh: 復為州別駕，辟司空郗鑒掾，除長山令。

translations.literal: Again he was prefecture aide-de-camp, summoned as Minister of Works Xi Jian's clerk, appointed magistrate of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as provincial aide-de-camp, was summoned as a clerk to Xi Jian the minister of works, and was appointed magistrate of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 鑒又請為司馬，轉黃門郎。

translations.literal: Jian again requested him as marshal; he was transferred to Yellow Gate Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jian later secured his appointment as marshal, after which he was transferred to gentleman at the yellow gates.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍庾冰鎮江州，請為長史。

translations.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Yu Bing garrisoned Jiangzhou, requested him as senior clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Bing, general of chariots and cavalry, took command at Jiangzhou, he named Jiang Bin his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 冰薨，庾翼以為諮議參軍，俄而復補長史。

translations.literal: Bing died; Yu Yi took him as consultation army adviser; shortly again supplemented as senior clerk.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu Bing died, Yu Yi appointed him advising staff officer, and soon restored him to the post of chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 翼薨，大將幹瓚作難，虨討平之。

translations.literal: Yi died; great general Gan Zan made difficulty; Bin punished and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Yi died, the general Gan Zan mutinied; Jiang Bin attacked him and restored order.

sentences.zh: 除尚書吏部郎，仍遷御史中丞、侍中、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Masters of Writing personnel department gentleman; still was promoted to imperial secretary central director, attendant-in-ordinary, Masters of Writing personnel minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of the personnel bureau of the masters of writing, then rose in succession to palace secretary, attendant-in-ordinary, and minister of the personnel bureau.

sentences.zh: 永和中，代桓景為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the Yonghe period, he replaced Huan Jing as General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghe era he succeeded Huan Jing as general who guards the army.

sentences.zh: 出補會稽內史，加右軍將軍。

translations.literal: He went out to supplement as Kuaiji interior history, added General of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital to serve as interior governor of Kuaiji with the additional title of general of the right army.

sentences.zh: 代王彪之為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: He replaced Wang Biaozhi as Masters of Writing vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded Wang Biaozhi as vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 哀帝即位，疑周貴人名號所宜，虨議見《禮志》。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ai ascended, doubting what was fitting for the Zhou honorable consort's titles, Bin's deliberation is seen in the Treatise on Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ai came to the throne, the court debated the proper titles for the Honored Lady Zhou; Jiang Bin's opinion is recorded in the Treatise on Rites.

sentences.zh: 帝欲於殿庭立鴻祀，又欲躬自藉田，虨並以為禮廢日久，儀注不存，中興以來所不行，謂宜停之。

translations.literal: The emperor desired in the palace courtyard to establish Hong sacrifice, and also desired personally himself to perform the ploughing field; Bin both thought the rites had been abandoned long, ritual notes not preserved, since the restoration not practiced, saying it was fit to stop them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to institute the great archery sacrifice in the court hall and to plough the sacred field himself; Jiang Bin held that both ceremonies had long fallen out of use, that the rubrics were lost, and that neither had been performed since the restoration—he urged that the plans be dropped.

sentences.zh: 為僕射積年，簡文帝為相，每訪政事，虨多所補益，轉護軍將軍，領國子祭酒，卒官。

translations.literal: As vice director accumulated years, Emperor Jianwen was minister, each time consulting government affairs, Bin had many supplements and benefits; he was transferred to General Who Guards the Army, concurrently libationer of the imperial academy, died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He served for years as vice director while Emperor Jianwen held the premiership; whenever policy was discussed, Jiang Bin's contributions were substantial. He was then made general who guards the army and concurrent libationer of the imperial academy, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子敳，曆琅邪內史、驃騎諮議。

translations.literal: Son Yin, successively Langye interior history, fierce cavalry consultation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiang Yin served in turn as interior governor of Langye and advising officer to the general of swift cavalry.

sentences.zh: 敳子恆，元熙中為西中郎長史。

translations.literal: Yin's son Heng, in the Yuanxi period was Western Central Gentleman senior clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's son Jiang Heng was chief clerk to the general of the western center during the Yuanxi era.

sentences.zh: 恆弟夷，尚書。

translations.literal: Heng's younger brother Yi, Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Heng's younger brother Jiang Yi rose to the post of masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 惇字思悛，孝友淳粹，高節邁俗。

translations.literal: Dun, courtesy name Sisun, filial and friendly pure and unmixed, high integrity surpassing custom.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Dun, courtesy name Sisun, was devoted to his family, gentle and unspoiled in character, and carried a moral seriousness that set him apart from the common run.

sentences.zh: 性好學，儒玄並綜。

translations.literal: His nature loved learning; Confucian and arcane both combined.
translations.idiomatic: He loved study and mastered both Confucian learning and arcane philosophy.

sentences.zh: 每以為君子立行，應依禮而動，雖隱顯殊途，未有不傍禮教者也。

translations.literal: He always thought that the noble man in establishing conduct ought to move according to rite; although hidden and displayed are different paths, there is none who does not lean on ritual teaching.
translations.idiomatic: He held that a gentleman orders his conduct by ritual, whether in office or in retirement, and that no upright path strays from the teachings of propriety.

sentences.zh: 若乃放達不羈，以肆縱為貴者，非但動違禮法，亦道之所棄也。
