translations.literal: As for those who are unrestrained and not bound, taking wanton license as noble—not only do their movements violate ritual law, they are also what the Way casts aside.
translations.idiomatic: Those who make a cult of wild abandon and count license as nobility violate not only decorum but the Way itself.

sentences.zh: 乃著《通道崇檢論》，世咸稱之。

translations.literal: Therefore he composed the "Discourse on Penetrating the Way and Honoring Restraint"; the age all praised it.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore wrote his treatise "On Penetrating the Way and Honoring Restraint," which won wide acclaim.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻之亂，避地東陽山，太尉郗鑒檄為兗州治中，又辟太尉掾；

translations.literal: In Su Jun's rebellion, he avoided the ground to Dongyang Mountain; Grand Commandant Xi Jian summoned him as Yanzhou administration supervisor, again summoned as Grand Commandant clerk;
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun rose in revolt, he took refuge on Mount Dongyang; Grand Commandant Xi Jian called him up as senior clerk of Yanzhou and then as clerk on the grand commandant's staff;

sentences.zh: 康帝為司徒，亦辟焉；

translations.literal: Emperor Kang was minister of education, also summoned him;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Kang, as minister of education, summoned him as well;

sentences.zh: 征西將軍庾亮請為儒林參軍；

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the West Yu Liang requested him as Confucian Forest army adviser;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang, general who conquers the west, offered him a post as adviser on scholarly affairs;

sentences.zh: 徵拜博士、著作郎，皆不就。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed erudite, editorial director; all he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as an academician and as editorial director, but he declined both appointments.

sentences.zh: 邑裏宗其道，有事必諮而後行。

translations.literal: The town and village honored his Way; when there was business they must consult and afterward act.
translations.idiomatic: His home district looked to him as a moral authority and would undertake nothing of weight without first seeking his counsel.

sentences.zh: 東陽太守阮裕、長山令王濛，皆一時名士，並與惇遊處，深相欽重。

translations.literal: Dongyang governor Ruan Yu, Changshan magistrate Wang Meng, were all one generation's famous scholars, and together with Dun wandered and dwelled, deeply mutually admiring and respecting.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yu, governor of Dongyang, and Wang Meng, magistrate of Changshan, were leading men of the day; both befriended Jiang Dun and held him in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 養志二十餘年，永和九年卒，時年四十九，友朋相與刊石立頌，以表德美雲。

translations.literal: He nourished his aims more than twenty years; in the ninth year of Yonghe he died, at the time age forty-nine; friends together carved stone and raised praise, thereby to display virtue's beauty.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated his aspirations in seclusion for more than twenty years and died in the ninth year of Yonghe at forty-nine; his friends joined to carve a stele in his honor and celebrate his virtue.

sentences.zh: 孫楚，字子荊，太原中都人也。

translations.literal: Sun Chu, courtesy name Zijing, was a man of Zhongdu in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chu, whose courtesy name was Zijing, came from Zhongdu in Taiyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖資，魏驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zi was Wei fierce cavalry general.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sun Zi had been general of swift cavalry under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父宏，南陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Hong was Nanyang governor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sun Hong served as governor of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 楚才藻卓絕，爽邁不群，多所陵傲，缺鄉曲之譽。

translations.literal: Chu's literary talent was outstanding and transcendent, bright and bold not grouping with others; much he insulted and was arrogant toward, lacking village and lane's praise.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chu was brilliantly gifted and fiercely independent; he looked down on others and won little goodwill in his home district.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，始參鎮東軍事。

translations.literal: Past forty, he first participated in the General Who Guards the East's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Not until his forties did he take a staff post with the general who guards the east.

sentences.zh: 文帝遣符劭、孫郁使吳，將軍石苞令楚作書遺孫皓曰：

translations.literal: Emperor Wen dispatched Fu Shao and Sun Yu as envoys to Wu; General Shi Bao ordered Chu to compose a letter to leave to Sun Hao, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen sent Fu Shao and Sun Yu as envoys to Wu, General Shi Bao instructed Sun Chu to draft a letter to Sun Hao. It read:

sentences.zh: 蓋見機而作，《周易》所貴；

translations.literal: Seeing the pivot and then acting is what the Zhou Changes esteems;
translations.idiomatic: To read the moment and act upon it is what the Book of Changes esteems;

sentences.zh: 小不事大，《春秋》所誅。

translations.literal: the small not serving the great is what the Spring and Autumn punishes.
translations.idiomatic: for the small to refuse service to the great is what the Spring and Autumn Annals condemn.

sentences.zh: 此乃吉凶之萌兆，榮辱所由生也。

translations.literal: This then is good and ill's sprouting omen, glory and shame whereby born.
translations.idiomatic: These are the first signs of fortune or ruin, the root of honor or disgrace.

sentences.zh: 是故許、鄭以銜璧全國，曹譚以無禮取滅。

translations.literal: Therefore Xu and Zheng by holding jade in mouth preserved the whole state; Cao and Tan by lacking ritual took destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the houses of Xu and Zheng saved their states whole by coming with jade tokens of submission, while Cao and Tan were wiped out for their arrogance.

sentences.zh: 載藉既記其成敗，古今又著其愚智，不復廣引譬類，崇飾浮辭。

translations.literal: Records already record their success and failure; past and present again display their foolish and wise; we do not again broadly cite analogies, exalt and adorn floating phrases.
translations.idiomatic: Histories already record how states rose and fell, and past and present show plainly which rulers were wise and which foolish; there is no need to pile up parallels or dress the matter in fine words.

sentences.zh: 苟以誇大為名，更喪忠告之實。

translations.literal: If by boasting greatness as name, further lose loyal counsel's substance.
translations.idiomatic: To seek only a grandiloquent name is to forfeit the substance of honest counsel.

sentences.zh: 今粗論事要，以相覺悟。

translations.literal: Now roughly discussing the affair's essentials, thereby mutually to awaken and realize.
translations.idiomatic: I shall therefore sketch the essentials of your situation in the hope of awakening you to the danger.

sentences.zh: 昔炎精幽昧，歷數將終，恆、靈失德，災釁並興，豺狼抗爪牙之毒，生靈罹塗炭之難。

translations.literal: Formerly the fire essence was dim and dark, the reckoned succession about to end; Huan and Ling lost virtue; disasters and omens together arose; jackals and wolves resisted claw and fang's poison; living spirits suffered mud and charcoal's hardship.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han fire virtue guttered and the dynasty's mandate neared its end, under Emperors Huan and Ling misrule brought calamity on every side; rebels showed their fangs and the people were trampled as if in mud and fire.

sentences.zh: 由是九州絕貫，王綱解紐，四海蕭條，非復漢有。

translations.literal: From this the nine provinces' thread snapped, the royal net's knot loosed, the four seas desolate, no longer again Han's possession.
translations.idiomatic: The nine regions were cut off from one another, imperial authority unraveled, and the realm lay waste—no longer the Han's domain.

sentences.zh: 太祖承運，神武應期，征討暴亂，克甯區夏；

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor received the movement, divine martial answered the period, punishing and attacking violent disorder, able to quiet the regional Xia;
translations.idiomatic: Our Grand Progenitor took up the mandate, his godlike might answered the times, and he crushed rebellion until the heartland was pacified;

sentences.zh: 協建靈符，天命既集，遂廓弘基，奄有魏域。

translations.literal: Harmoniously establishing spirit tallies, Heaven's mandate already gathered, thereupon broadened the great foundation, covered and possessed Wei's domain.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's omens aligned, the mandate was gathered in, and he widened the great foundation until he held all the territory of Wei.

sentences.zh: 土則神州中嶽，器則九鼎猶存，世載淑美，重光相襲，故知四隩之攸同，帝者之壯觀也。

translations.literal: In soil then the divine continent's central peak; in vessels then the nine tripods still exist; generations bearing fine beauty, repeated light mutually inheriting; therefore know the four remote quarters' sameness—this is the emperor's grand sight.
translations.idiomatic: His realm spans the sacred central peak of the Chinese world; the nine tripods, token of sovereignty, are still in his care; generation after generation his house has piled virtue upon virtue—so the four quarters are one again, a spectacle fit for an emperor.

sentences.zh: 昔公孫氏承藉父兄，世居東裔，擁帶燕胡，憑陵險遠，講武遊盤，不供職貢，內傲帝命，外通南國，乘桴滄海，交酬貨賄，葛越布於朔土，貂馬延于吳會；

translations.literal: Formerly the Gongsun clan relied on father and elder brothers, generation dwelling in the eastern fringe, girding Yan and Hu, relying on peril and distance, lecturing martial and roaming and circling, not supplying tribute duty, inwardly arrogant to imperial command, outwardly communicating with the southern state, riding rafts on the dark sea, exchanging goods and bribes, Ge-Yue cloth spread in the northern soil, sable horses extending to Wu and Gui;
translations.idiomatic: The Gongsun house of Liaodong, inheriting power from father and brother, long held the eastern march, ringed themselves with Yan and Hu auxiliaries, trusted in distance and rugged terrain, drilled troops for sport, withheld tribute, defied the court within while trading with the south beyond the sea, shuttling bribes across the waves until Yue cloth filled the north and Wu sables reached the steppe;

sentences.zh: 自以控弦十萬，奔走之力，信能右折燕、齊，左震扶桑，輮轢沙漠，南面稱王。

translations.literal: They self-thought string-drawers hundred thousand, running's force, truly able right to break Yan and Qi, left to shake Fusang, crush and roll the sand desert, south-facing to call themselves kings.
translations.idiomatic: they fancied that a hundred thousand bowmen and swift cavalry could break Yan and Qi to the west, thunder against Fusang to the east, ride roughshod over the deserts, and face south as kings.

sentences.zh: 宣王薄伐，猛銳長驅，師次遼陽，而城池不守；

translations.literal: King Xuan lightly campaigned; fierce and sharp long drove; the army halted at Liaoyang, yet walls and moats did not hold;
translations.idiomatic: King Xuan of Wei struck lightly but drove deep; his host reached Liaoyang, and their walls could not hold;

sentences.zh: 枹鼓暫鳴，而元凶折首。

translations.literal: Drum and drumstick briefly sounded, and the chief villain broke head.
translations.idiomatic: the drums had hardly sounded when the rebel chief lost his head.

sentences.zh: 於是遠近疆埸，列郡大荒，收離聚散，大安其居，眾庶悅服，殊俗款附。

translations.literal: Thereupon far and near border fields, arrayed commanderies greatly waste, gathering parted and scattering gathered, greatly peace their dwellings; the masses joyfully submitted; alien customs sincerely attached.
translations.idiomatic: Border counties far and near lay in ruin until the scattered were gathered home, the people given peace, common folk and barbarians alike gladly submitted.

sentences.zh: 自茲以降，九野清泰，東夷獻其樂器，肅慎貢其楛矢，曠世不羈，應化而至，巍巍蕩蕩，想所具聞也。

translations.literal: From this downward, the nine fields clear and peaceful, eastern Yi presented their musical instruments, Sushen offered their wooden arrows, ages apart not bound, answering transformation and arriving; lofty and vast—presumably you have all heard.
translations.idiomatic: Since then the nine domains have known peace: eastern tribes have sent their instruments, the Sushen their arrow-shafts, and peoples long outside the pale have answered civilization and come in—all this, in its majesty, is surely known to you.

sentences.zh: 吳之先祖，起自荊、楚，遭時擾攘，潛播江表。

translations.literal: Wu's ancestor spirits rose from Jing and Chu, met times of disturbance and turmoil, secretly spread beyond the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: The founders of Wu rose from the Jing-Chu country in an age of chaos and slipped their power across the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 劉備震懼，亦逃巴、岷。

translations.literal: Liu Bei trembled in fear, also fled to Ba and Min.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei broke in panic and fled into Ba and Min.

sentences.zh: 遂因山陵積石之固，三江五湖浩汗無涯，假氣遊魂，迄茲四紀。

translations.literal: Thereupon relying on mountains and mounds piled stone's firmness, three rivers and five lakes vast and boundless, borrowing breath wandering souls, down to here four periods of twelve years.
translations.idiomatic: They trusted in heaped stone and mountain barriers, in the boundless maze of the three rivers and five lakes, and clung to borrowed legitimacy like wandering ghosts for nearly half a century.

sentences.zh: 兩邦合從，東西唱和，互相扇動，距捍中國。

translations.literal: Two states joined vertical alliance, east and west chanting response, mutually fanning and moving, resisting and guarding the Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: The two kingdoms leagued east and west, echoing each other's defiance and stiffening one another against the Chinese heartland.

sentences.zh: 自謂三分鼎足之勢，可與泰山共相終始也。

translations.literal: They self-called a three-part tripod-foot situation, able with Mount Tai mutually to end and begin.
translations.idiomatic: They imagined a tripod of three legs that might stand as long as Mount Tai itself.

sentences.zh: 相國晉王輔相帝室，文武桓桓，志厲秋霜，廟勝之算，應變無窮，獨見之鑒，與眾絕慮。

translations.literal: Chancellor Jin Wang assisted the imperial house; civil and military awe-inspiring; aims honed like autumn frost; temple victory's reckoning, answering change without end; alone-seeing's mirror, with the masses severed in thought.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin king, as imperial chancellor, aids the throne; his civil and military officers are a formidable host, their resolution sharp as autumn frost; his plans win victory in the council hall and meet every shift of fortune; his foresight leaves ordinary counsel far behind.

sentences.zh: 主上欽明，委以萬機，長轡遠禦，妙略潛授，偏師同心，上下用力，陵威奮伐，罙入其阻，并敵一向，奪其膽氣。

translations.literal: The lord above is reverent and bright, entrusting him the myriad pivots; long reins far controlling, subtle stratagems secretly given; detached armies one heart, above and below exerting force; pressing might striving campaign, deeply entering their obstructions, joining the enemy in one direction, seizing their gall and breath.
translations.idiomatic: Our reverent sovereign has entrusted him with every thread of policy; he holds the long reins, issues secret orders, and moves detached columns as one body so that high and low strain together—his majesty advances, pierces their strongholds, strikes them on a single front, and breaks their nerve.

sentences.zh: 小戰江由，則成都自潰；

translations.literal: A small battle at Jiangyou, then Chengdu of itself collapsed;
translations.idiomatic: A brief clash at Jiangyou, and Chengdu collapsed of its own accord;

sentences.zh: 曜兵劍閣，則姜維面縛。

translations.literal: Displaying troops at Sword Gate, then Jiang Wei face-bound.
translations.idiomatic: a display of arms at Sword Gate, and Jiang Wei came bound with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 開地六千，領郡三十。

translations.literal: Opened territory six thousand, leading commanderies thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Six thousand square li of territory were opened and thirty commanderies brought under the flag.

sentences.zh: 兵不逾時，梁、益肅清，使竊號之雄，稽顙絳闕，球琳重錦，充於府庫。

translations.literal: Weapons not exceeding the season, Liang and Yi were cleared; causing the heroes who stole titles to knock foreheads at the crimson gate; ball-jade and layered brocade filled the treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: Before a year was out Liang and Yi were swept clean; the warlord who had usurped a royal title knocked his brow at the palace gate, and precious jades and brocades filled the Wei storehouses.

sentences.zh: 夫韓並魏徙，虢滅虞亡，此皆前鑒，後事之表。

translations.literal: Han annexed and Wei moved; Guo extinguished, Yu perished—these all are former mirrors, later affairs' model.
translations.idiomatic: When Han swallowed rival states and Wei shifted its capital, when Guo fell and Yu followed to ruin—these are lessons the histories have already written plain for later ages.

sentences.zh: 又南中呂興，深睹天命蟬蛻內附，願為臣妾。

translations.literal: Moreover in the south within Lu Xing, deeply seeing Heaven's mandate, cicada-sloughed and inward attached, willing to be minister and concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Lü Xing in the south, reading Heaven's will aright, has cast off Shu like a cicada shell and submitted, begging to rank as a subject.

sentences.zh: 外失輔車脣齒之援，內有羽毛零落之漸，而徘徊危國，冀延日月，此由魏武侯卻指山河，自以為強，殊不知物有興亡，則所美非其地也。

translations.literal: Without losing chariot-and-carriage lip-and-teeth aid, within having feather-and-down scattering and falling's gradualness, yet lingering in a perilous state, hoping to extend days and months—this is from Marquis Wu of Wei pointing at mountains and rivers, self-thinking strong, utterly not knowing things have rise and perish, then what is prized is not its ground.
translations.idiomatic: You have lost the outer support that locked Shu and Wu like lips to teeth; within, your own wings are molting one by one; yet you linger in a doomed kingdom hoping to buy a few more days—like Marquis Wu of Wei boasting over his rivers and mountains, blind to the truth that power rises and falls and that what he prized was not truly his to keep.

sentences.zh: 方今百僚濟濟，俊乂盈朝，武臣猛將，折沖萬里，國富兵強，六軍精練，思復翰飛，飲馬南海。

translations.literal: Just now the hundred officials in array, outstanding men fill the court; martial ministers fierce generals, repel enemies ten thousand li; the state rich, weapons strong, the six armies refined and drilled, thinking again to brush and fly, drinking horses in the South Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Today the court teems with able men, fierce generals hold the enemy at bay a thousand miles away, the treasury is full and the six hosts are hardened for war, eager to spread their wings and water their horses in the southern sea.

sentences.zh: 自頃國家整修器械，興造舟楫，簡習水戰，樓船萬艘，千里相望，刳木已來，舟車之用未有如今之殷盛者也。

translations.literal: Since recently the state has repaired and ordered weapons and tools, raised and built boats and oars, selected and drilled water warfare; towered ships ten thousand vessels, a thousand li mutually gazing; since hollowing wood, boats and chariots' use has never been as abundant and flourishing as now.
translations.idiomatic: The state has lately refitted arms, built fleets, drilled river warfare, and launched myriads of tower ships that stretch in sight of one another for a thousand li—never since men first hollowed logs for boats have water and land transport been readied on such a scale.

sentences.zh: 驍勇百萬，畜力待時。

translations.literal: Fierce braves a million, storing strength awaiting the moment.
translations.idiomatic: A million veterans stand by, hoarding their strength for the chosen hour.

sentences.zh: 役不再舉，今日之師也。

translations.literal: Service not twice raised—this is today's host.
translations.idiomatic: The next campaign will not need a second levy: the host is ready today.

sentences.zh: 然主相眷眷未便電發者，猶以為愛人治國，道家所尚，崇城遂卑，文王退舍，故先開大信，喻以存亡，殷勤之指，往使所究也。

translations.literal: Yet lord and minister lingering have not then lightning-launched, still taking cherishing men and ordering the state as what the Dao school esteems; exalting the city wall, then yielding low; King Wen withdrew encampment; therefore first opening great trust, instructing by survival and perish, earnest and diligent's intent—what the departing envoys exhaust.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ruler and chancellor have held back from striking like lightning because they prize the Daoist maxim of cherishing the people: as King Wen once raised his siege works high only to dismantle them and withdraw, they first offer you utmost good faith and send envoys to explain life and death—this is the burden our messengers bear.

sentences.zh: 若能審勢安危，自求多福，蹶然改容，祗承往錫，追慕南越，嬰齊入侍，北面稱臣，伏聽告策，則世祚江表，永為魏籓，豐功顯報，隆於今日矣。

translations.literal: If able to examine the situation's danger and safety, self-seek much fortune, suddenly change countenance, respectfully receive past grace, trace and admire Southern Yue, Yingqi entering attendance, north-facing calling themselves ministers, bowing to hear proclaimed strategy, then generations' blessing south of the Yangtze, forever being Wei's fence, rich merit and manifest reward, exalted beyond today.
translations.idiomatic: If you read the danger aright and choose the better fortune—if you change your bearing, accept past kindness, follow the example of Southern Yue when its king sent his heir to wait on the Han court, face north as a vassal, and bow to receive the edict—your line may keep the south of the river forever as Wei's bulwark, and your reward will tower above anything you enjoy today.

sentences.zh: 若猶侮慢，未順王命，然後謀力雲合，指麾從風，雍、梁二州，順流而東，青、徐戰士，列江而西，荊、揚兗、豫，爭驅八沖，征東甲卒，武步秣陵，爾乃王輿整駕，六戎徐征，羽校燭日，旌旗星流，龍游曜路，歌吹盈耳，士卒奔邁，其會如林，煙塵俱起，震天駭地，渴賞之士，鋒鏑爭先，忽然一旦，身首橫分，宗祀淪覆，取戒萬世，引領南望，良助寒心！

translations.literal: If still insulting and slow, not obeying the king's command, then afterward stratagem and strength cloud-gather, signal and banner follow wind; Yong and Liang two provinces, along the current eastward; Qing and Xu warriors, arrayed along the river westward; Jing, Yang, Yan, Yu, racing to drive the eight thoroughfares; east-campaigning mailed soldiers, martially stepping Moling; then the king's chariot arrays harness, six hosts slowly campaign, feathered companies candle the sun, banners and flags star-stream; dragons roam shining the road, songs and flutes fill the ear; soldiers and foot race, their assembly like forest; smoke and dust together rise, shaking heaven and startling earth; thirst-rewarding knights, point and arrow vying first; suddenly one dawn, body and head cross-split; ancestral sacrifice sunk and overturned, taking warning for ten thousand generations—stretching neck southward gazing, truly aiding cold heart!
translations.idiomatic: If you cling to arrogance and defy the king's command, then every plan and weapon will mass like a cloud: Yong and Liang will sweep downriver to the east, Qing and Xu veterans line the western shore, hosts from Jing, Yang, Yan, and Yu thunder through every pass, and the eastern expedition's mail-clad ranks march on Moling until the imperial carriages form line, the six armies advance at a steady pace, pennons outshine the sun, banners stream like meteors, chariots roll like dragons in glittering files, and music fills the air—soldiers will rush to the rendezvous thick as a forest, dust will blot heaven and earth, every man hungry for reward will strain to be first at the spears, and in one morning your head may part from your body, your altars fall, and you become a warning for ages—stretch your neck toward the south and you will know enough to shudder!

sentences.zh: 夫療膏肓之疾者，必進苦口之藥；

translations.literal: Now treating gao-huang's illness must advance bitter mouth's medicine;
translations.idiomatic: A disease in the vitals calls for bitter medicine;

sentences.zh: 決狐疑之慮者，亦告逆耳之言。

translations.literal: Deciding fox-doubt's anxiety also tells ear-offending words.
translations.idiomatic: to cut through doubt one must speak unwelcome truth.

sentences.zh: 如其猶豫，迷而不反，恐俞附見其已死，扁鵲知其無功矣。

translations.literal: If like this hesitating, lost and not returning, I fear Yu Fu will see them already dead, Bian Que will know there is no merit.
translations.idiomatic: If you hesitate still, lost past turning back, even Yu Fu will pronounce the corpse beyond saving and Bian Que will decline the case as hopeless.

sentences.zh: 勉思良圖，惟所去就。

translations.literal: Strive to think a good plan; only as to going or staying.
translations.idiomatic: Think hard on a wise course and choose your path.

sentences.zh: 劭等至吳，不敢為通。

translations.literal: Shao and the others reached Wu, did not dare to communicate for them.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Shao and his party reached Wu, no one dared pass the letter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 楚後遷佐著作郎，復參石苞驃騎軍事。

translations.literal: Chu afterward was transferred to assistant editorial director, again participated in Shi Bao's fierce cavalry military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chu was later promoted to assistant editorial director and again served on the staff of Shi Bao, general of swift cavalry.

sentences.zh: 楚既負其材氣，頗侮易於苞，初至，長揖曰：「天子命我參卿軍事。

translations.literal: Chu having relied on his talent and qi, rather insulted and treated lightly Bao; on first arrival, long bowed and said: "The Son of Heaven ordered me to participate in your excellency's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his gifts, Sun Chu treated Shi Bao with thinly veiled contempt; on his first day he made only a standing bow and said, "The Son of Heaven has ordered me to join your staff.

sentences.zh: 」因此而嫌隙遂構。

translations.literal: " From this therefore rancor and crack were constructed.
translations.idiomatic: " From that moment bad blood grew between them.

sentences.zh: 苞奏楚與吳人孫世山共訕毀時政，楚亦抗表自理，紛紜經年，事未判，又與鄉人郭奕忿爭。

translations.literal: Bao memorialized that Chu together with Wu man Sun Shishan jointly slandered current government; Chu also submitted counter-memorial self-justifying; confusedly for a year the affair was not decided; again with fellow townsman Guo Yi he quarreled in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bao reported that Sun Chu had slandered the court together with a Wu man named Sun Shishan; Sun Chu answered with a memorial in his own defense; the wrangle dragged on a year without verdict, and he also fell into a bitter quarrel with his townsman Guo Yi.

sentences.zh: 武帝雖不顯明其罪，然以少賤受責，遂湮廢積年。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu although did not openly clarify his crime, yet because he slighted his superior in youth he received blame, thereupon sank and was discarded many years.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu never formally declared him guilty, yet because he had slighted his commander he was left in disgrace for years.

sentences.zh: 初，參軍不敬府主，楚既輕苞，遂制施敬，自楚始也。

translations.literal: At first, army advisers did not respect the prefectural chief; Chu having slighted Bao, thereupon was established the practice of showing respect—beginning from Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Until then staff officers had not been required to defer to their commanders; because Sun Chu had insulted Shi Bao, a rule was laid down that they must show respect—a reform that began with Sun Chu.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍，扶風王駿與楚舊好，起為參軍。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the West, Prince of Fufeng Jun with Chu old friendship, raised him as army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jun, the Prince of Fufeng and general who conquers the west, was an old friend of Sun Chu and had him brought out of retirement as an army adviser.

sentences.zh: 轉梁令，遷衛將軍司馬，時龍見武庫井中，群臣將上賀，楚上言曰：「頃聞武庫井中有二龍，群臣或有謂之禎祥而稱賀者，或有謂之非祥無所賀者，可謂楚既失之，而齊亦未為得也。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Liang magistrate, promoted to Guard General's marshal; at the time dragons appeared in the arsenal well; the host of ministers were about to ascend congratulations; Chu submitted words saying: "Recently I heard that in the arsenal well there are two dragons; among the host of ministers some call it auspicious portent and offer congratulations, some call it not auspicious and offer no congratulations—one may say Chu already missed it, yet Qi also was not entirely right.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Liang and promoted to marshal to the guard general. When two dragons were seen in the arsenal well and the ministers prepared to congratulate the throne, Sun Chu submitted a memorial: "I have lately heard of two dragons in the arsenal well. Some ministers call it a good omen and would congratulate Your Majesty; others deny that it is auspicious and would not congratulate. One might say that Chu was wrong in its reading, but Qi was not entirely right either.

sentences.zh: 夫龍或俯鱗潛於重泉，或仰攀雲漢遊乎蒼昊，而今蟠于坎井，同於蛙蝦者，豈獨管庫之士或有隱伏，廝役之賢沒于行伍？

translations.literal: Now dragons sometimes fold scales and lurk in doubled springs, sometimes climb the Milky Way and roam in the blue vault; yet now they coil in a pit well, the same as frogs and shrimp—how can it be only that arsenal clerks perhaps have hidden worth, menial service worthies sunk in the ranks?
translations.idiomatic: Dragons may hide their scales in the deepest pools or climb the Milky Way in the open sky; to find them coiled in a well like frogs and mudfish—does this mean only that some clerk in the armory has hidden talent, or that worthy men of low station languish among the ranks?

sentences.zh: 故龍見光景，有所感悟。

translations.literal: Therefore the dragon's appearing in light and scene has something to awaken and touch.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon's appearance is a sign meant to stir reflection.

sentences.zh: 願陛下赦小過，舉賢才，垂夢于傅岩，望想於渭濱，修學官，起淹滯，申命公卿，舉獨行君子可惇風厲俗者，又舉亮拔秀異之才可以撥煩理難矯世抗言者，無系世族，必先逸賤。

translations.literal: We hope Your Majesty will pardon small faults, raise worthy talents, let fall dream on Fu's cliff, gaze and think on Wei's bank, repair study halls, raise the submerged and stuck, reissue orders to dukes and ministers to raise solitary-practice gentlemen who can thicken custom and sharpen vulgar ways, and again raise bright and plucked outstanding unusual talents able to sort tangles, order difficulties, correct the age and speak boldly—not bound to noble clans, must first take the retired and base.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty will overlook petty faults, promote worthy men, dream as Wu Ding dreamed of a sage at Fu Rock, look as King Wen looked beside the Wei River, restore the schools, lift the blocked and forgotten, command the high ministers to recommend recluses whose conduct can improve the age, and men of outstanding talent who can cut through tangles, set chaos right, and speak truth to power—without confining the search to great families, and looking first among the humble and overlooked.

sentences.zh: 夫戰勝攻取之勢，並兼混一之威，五伯之事，韓、白之功耳；

translations.literal: Now the momentum of battle victory and attack capture, the awe of annexing and mixing into one—the Five Hegemons' affairs, Han and Bai's merit only;
translations.idiomatic: The work of conquest and the glory of uniting the realm belong to the Five Hegemons and to captains like Han Xin and Bai Qi;

sentences.zh: 至於制禮作樂，闡揚道化，甫是士人出筋力之秋也。

translations.literal: Reaching to regulating rites and making music, opening and raising the Way's transformation—this is just the season for scholars to extend sinew and strength.
translations.idiomatic: but to set rites and music in order and spread the transforming power of the Way is the season in which men of learning must bend their strength.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下擇狂夫之言。」

translations.literal: We bow wishing Your Majesty to choose the mad fellow's words."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to heed even the wild words of a humble subject."

sentences.zh: 惠帝初，為馮翊太守。

translations.literal: At Emperor Hui's beginning, he was Fufeng governor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Hui's reign he became governor of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 元康三年卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuankang he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of the Yuankang era.

sentences.zh: 初，楚與同郡王濟友善，濟為本州大中正，訪問銓邑人品狀，至楚，濟曰：「此人非卿所能目，吾自為之。

translations.literal: At first, Chu with same commandery Wang Ji was friendly and good; Ji was the prefecture's grand rectifier, visiting and inquiring and evaluating the town's persons' character descriptions; when it reached Chu, Ji said: "This person is not what you can eye; I will myself do it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chu was on good terms with Wang Ji of his commandery. When Wang Ji served as grand rectifier for the province and was reviewing local character ratings, he came to Sun Chu and said, "This man is beyond your judgment; I shall write his evaluation myself.

sentences.zh: 」乃狀楚曰：「天才英博，亮拔不群。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he described Chu saying: "Heavenly talent heroic and vast, bright and plucked, not grouping with others.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore wrote of Sun Chu: "Heaven-given genius, heroic breadth, outstanding and peerless.

sentences.zh: 」楚少時欲隱居，謂濟曰：「當欲枕石漱流。

translations.literal: " Chu in youth wished to dwell in reclusion, saying to Ji: "I intend to pillow on stone and rinse mouth with flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: " In his youth Sun Chu wished to retire from the world and told Wang Ji, "I mean to use a rock for my pillow and rinse my mouth in a stream.

sentences.zh: 」誤云「漱石枕流」。

translations.literal: " Mistakenly he said "rinse mouth with stone, pillow on flowing water."
translations.idiomatic: " He misspoke as "rinse my mouth with stone and pillow on the current."

sentences.zh: 濟曰：「流非可枕，石非可漱。

translations.literal: " Ji said: "Flowing water is not what can be pillowed; stone is not what can be rinsed.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Ji replied, "You cannot pillow on a current, nor rinse your teeth with a stone.

sentences.zh: 」楚曰：「所以枕流，欲洗其耳；

translations.literal: " Chu said: "The reason I pillow on flowing water is desiring to wash the ears;
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Chu said, "I pillow on the current to wash my ears

sentences.zh: 所以漱石，欲厲其齒。

translations.literal: the reason I rinse with stone is desiring to grind the teeth.
translations.idiomatic: and I rinse with stone to sharpen my teeth.

sentences.zh: 」楚少所推服，惟雅敬濟。

translations.literal: " Chu seldom in whom he pushed submission, only elegantly respected Ji.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Chu rarely looked up to anyone, but he honored Wang Ji deeply.

sentences.zh: 初，楚除婦服，作詩以示濟，濟曰：「未知文生於情，情生於文，覽之淒然，增伉儷之重。」

translations.literal: At first, Chu removed wife mourning, composed a poem to show Ji; Ji said: "I did not know that wen is born from qing, qing is born from wen; reading it mournful, increasing the weight of husband-wife bond."
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Chu ended mourning for his wife, he showed Wang Ji a poem he had written. Wang Ji said, "I never knew whether feeling begets the words or the words beget the feeling; reading this, I am moved to sorrow and feel more deeply the bond of marriage."

sentences.zh: 三子：眾、洵、纂。

translations.literal: Three sons: Zhong, Xun, Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Sun Zhong, Sun Xun, and Sun Zuan.

sentences.zh: 眾及洵俱未仕而早終，惟纂子統、綽並知名。

translations.literal: Zhong and Xun both had not entered office and died early; only Zuan's sons Tong and Chuo together were known by name.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhong and Sun Xun died young without ever serving; only the sons of Sun Zuan, Sun Tong and Sun Chuo, won renown.

sentences.zh: 統字承公。

translations.literal: Tong, courtesy name Chenggong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tong, courtesy name Chenggong.

sentences.zh: 幼與綽及從弟盛過江。

translations.literal: In youth together with Chuo and paternal cousin Sheng crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he crossed the Yangtze with Sun Chuo and his cousin Sun Sheng.

sentences.zh: 誕任不羈，而善屬文，時人以為有楚風。

translations.literal: He was unrestrained and not bound, yet good at composing wen; people of the time thought he had Chu's wind.
translations.idiomatic: He was wildly unconventional and a fine writer; his contemporaries thought he had his father's dash.

sentences.zh: 征北將軍褚裒聞其名，命為參軍，辭不就，家於會稽。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the North Chu Pou heard his name, ordered him as army adviser; he declined and did not go, made home in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pou, general who conquers the north, heard of him and offered him a staff post, but he declined and settled in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 性好山水，乃求為鄞令，轉在吳寧。

translations.literal: His nature loved mountains and waters; thereupon sought to be Yin magistrate, was transferred to be in Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: He loved landscape and therefore sought appointment as magistrate of Yin, then was transferred to Wuning.

sentences.zh: 居職不留心碎務，縱意遊肆，名山勝川，靡不窮究。

translations.literal: Dwelling in office did not leave heart in fragmentary tasks; letting intent roam and wander, famous mountains and winning rivers, none not exhaustively investigated.
translations.idiomatic: In office he spared no attention to petty paperwork but gave himself to wandering; there was hardly a famous peak or stream he did not explore to the end.

sentences.zh: 後為余姚令，卒。

translations.literal: Afterward he was Yuyao magistrate, died.
translations.idiomatic: He later became magistrate of Yuyao and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 子騰嗣，以博學著稱，位至廷尉。

translations.literal: Son Teng succeeded; by broad learning was famed, rank reached commandant of justice.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Teng succeeded him, was known for wide scholarship, and rose to commandant of justice.

sentences.zh: 騰弟登，少善名理，注《老子》，行於世，仕至尚書郎，早終。

translations.literal: Teng's younger brother Deng, in youth good at name and pattern, annotated the Laozi, circulated in the world, office reached Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, died early.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng's younger brother Sun Deng was adept in youth at logical disputation, wrote a commentary on the Laozi that circulated widely, reached the post of gentleman of the masters of writing, and died young.

sentences.zh: 纂子綽

translations.literal: Zuan's son Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuo, son of Sun Zuan.

sentences.zh: 綽字興公。

translations.literal: Chuo, courtesy name Xinggong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuo, whose courtesy name was Xinggong.

sentences.zh: 博學善屬文，少與高陽許詢俱有高尚之志。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and good at composing wen; in youth together with Gaoyang Xu Xun both had lofty and high aims.
translations.idiomatic: He was widely read and a fine writer; in youth he and Xu Xun of Gaoyang shared a determination to live above vulgar ambition.

sentences.zh: 居於會稽，遊放山水，十有餘年，乃作《遂初賦》以致其意。

translations.literal: Dwelling in Kuaiji, roaming and releasing among mountains and waters more than ten years, then composed the "Rhapsody on Finding Life's First Intent" to convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Kuaiji for more than ten years, wandering among hills and streams, then wrote his rhapsody "On Finding Life's First Intent" to express his mind.

sentences.zh: 嘗鄙山濤，而謂人曰：「山濤吾所不解，吏非吏，隱非隱，若以元禮門為龍津，則當點額暴鱗矣。

translations.literal: He once despised Shan Tao, and said to people: "Shan Tao is what I do not understand—not official yet not official, not recluse yet not recluse; if he took Yuanli's gate as the dragon ford, then he ought to have dotted forehead and exposed scales.
translations.idiomatic: He once spoke slightingly of Shan Tao, saying, "I cannot make sense of Shan Tao—neither fish nor fowl, neither in office nor out of it; if he took Li Ying's threshold for the dragon gate, he would be the carp that burned its brow and never leaped the torrent."

sentences.zh: 」所居齋前種一株松，恆自守護，鄰人謂之曰：「樹子非不楚楚可憐，但恐永無棟樑日耳。

translations.literal: " Before his study he planted one pine tree, always personally guarding it; a neighbor said to him: "The tree is not that it is not clear and clear pitiable, but I fear it will never have a ridge-beam day.
translations.idiomatic: " Before his studio he planted a single pine and tended it himself. A neighbor told him, "The sapling is pretty enough, but I fear it will never see the day it serves as a beam."

sentences.zh: 」綽答曰：「楓柳雖復合抱，亦何所施邪！

translations.literal: " Chuo answered saying: "Maple and willow although again girth-encircling, what use are they!
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Chuo replied, "Maples and willows may grow thick as an embrace—what good are they for timber!"

sentences.zh: 」綽與詢一時名流，或愛詢高邁，則鄙於綽，或愛綽才藻，而無取於詢。

translations.literal: " Chuo and Xun were one generation's famous currents; some who loved Xun's high transcendence then despised Chuo; some who loved Chuo's literary talent then took nothing from Xun.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Chuo and Xu Xun were the leading lights of their day: some who admired Xu's lofty detachment looked down on Chuo, while others who prized Chuo's brilliance dismissed Xu."

sentences.zh: 沙門支遁試問綽：「君何如許？

translations.literal: The monk Zhi Dun tried asking Chuo: "How do you compare to Xu?
translations.idiomatic: The monk Zhi Dun once asked Sun Chuo, "How do you rank beside Xu Xun?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「高情遠致，弟子早已伏膺；

translations.literal: " He answered saying: "In high feeling and far-reaching aim, your disciple long ago bowed the breast;
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "In depth of mind and reach of vision I have long bowed to him;

sentences.zh: 然一詠一吟，許將北面矣。

translations.literal: yet in one chant one recitation, Xu will face north.
translations.idiomatic: yet in poetry and song he would face north to me as the lesser."

sentences.zh: 」絕重張衡、左思之賦，每云：「《三都》、《二京》，五經之鼓吹也。

translations.literal: " He utterly esteemed Zhang Heng's and Zuo Si's rhapsodies, always saying: "The Three Capitals and Two Capitals are the five classics' drum and wind.
translations.idiomatic: " He ranked the rhapsodies of Zhang Heng and Zuo Si above all others, declaring that the Three Capitals and Two Metropolises were the drum and fife that proclaimed the Five Classics."

sentences.zh: 」嘗作《天臺山賦》，辭致甚工，初成，以示友人范榮期，云：「卿試擲地，當作金石聲也。

translations.literal: " He once composed the "Rhapsody on Mount Tiantai"; its phrasing was very fine; when first finished, he showed it to his friend Fan Rongqi, saying: "You try throwing it to the ground—it ought to make metal and stone sound.
translations.idiomatic: " He once finished his "Rhapsody on Mount Tiantai," a piece of consummate craft, and showed it to his friend Fan Rongqi, saying, "Throw it on the ground—it should ring like bronze or stone."

sentences.zh: 」榮期曰：「恐此金石非中宮商。

translations.literal: " Rongqi said: "I fear this metal and stone is not centered in gong and shang.
translations.idiomatic: " Fan Rongqi replied, "I fear this metal and stone is off key."

sentences.zh: 」然每至佳句，輒云：「應是我輩語。

translations.literal: " Yet whenever reaching fine lines, then said: "This ought to be our sort's language.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet whenever he came to a fine line he would say, "That must be one of ours."

sentences.zh: 」除著作佐郎，襲爵長樂侯。」

translations.literal: " He was appointed assistant editorial director, inherited the title marquis of Changle."
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed assistant editorial director and succeeded to the title of marquis of Changle."

sentences.zh: 綽性通率，好譏調。

translations.literal: Chuo's nature was open and frank, fond of ridicule and teasing.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuo was blunt and outspoken and loved a sharp jest.

sentences.zh: 嘗與習鑿齒共行，綽在前，顧謂鑿齒曰：「沙之汰之，瓦石在後。

translations.literal: He once walked together with Xi Zuochi; Chuo was in front, turned and said to Zuochi: "What is sifted and washed, tiles and stones come behind.
translations.idiomatic: Walking once with Xi Zuochi, Sun Chuo took the lead, looked back, and said, "When sand is sifted, the gravel falls to the rear."

sentences.zh: 」鑿齒曰：「簸之揚之，糠秕在前。」

translations.literal: " Zuochi said: "What is winnowed and tossed, chaff and bran come in front."
translations.idiomatic: " Xi Zuochi shot back, "When grain is winnowed, the chaff flies to the front."

sentences.zh: 征西將軍庾亮請為參軍，補章安令，徵拜太學博士，遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the West Yu Liang requested him as army adviser; he was supplemented as Zhang'an magistrate; summoned and appointed grand academy erudite; promoted to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang, general who conquers the west, took him on as an army adviser; he was then named magistrate of Zhang'an, summoned as an erudite of the imperial academy, and promoted to gentleman of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 楊州刺史殷浩以為建威長史。

translations.literal: Yangzhou Inspector Yin Hao took him as bulwark-of-power senior clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao, inspector of Yangzhou, appointed him senior clerk to the general who establishes might.

sentences.zh: 會稽內史王羲之引為右軍長史。

translations.literal: Kuaiji interior history Wang Xizhi drew him in as Right Army senior clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xizhi, interior governor of Kuaiji, brought him in as chief clerk to the general of the right army.

sentences.zh: 轉永嘉太守，遷散騎常侍，領著作郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Yongjia governor, promoted to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, concurrently editorial director.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Yongjia, then promoted to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and concurrent editorial director.

sentences.zh: 時大司馬桓溫欲經緯中國，以河南粗平，將移都洛陽。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Marshal Huan Wen wished to order all under Heaven within China; because the Henan region was roughly pacified, he was about to move the capital to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Huan Wen wished to reorder the realm; with the Henan region south of the Yellow River roughly pacified, he proposed moving the capital to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 朝廷畏溫，不敢為異，而北土蕭條，人情疑懼，雖並知不可，莫敢先諫。

translations.literal: The court feared Wen, did not dare make opposition; yet the northern soil was desolate, human feelings doubtful and fearful; although all together knew it could not be, none dared first to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: The court feared Huan Wen and voiced no dissent, yet the north was a waste and the people were anxious; though everyone knew the scheme was folly, no one dared speak first.

sentences.zh: 綽乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: Chuo thereupon submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chu therefore addressed a memorial:

sentences.zh: 伏見征西大將軍臣溫表「便當躬率三軍，討除二寇，蕩滌河、渭，清灑舊京，然後神旂電舒，朝服濟江，反皇居於中土，正玉衡於天極。

translations.literal: We have seen General Who Conquers the West, great general, minister Wen's memorial: "I shall then personally lead the three armies, punish and remove the two bandits, wash clear the He and Wei, sprinkle clean the old capital; then divine banners lightning-extend, court dress cross the river, return the imperial dwelling to the central soil, set the jade sighting-tube at heaven's pole.
translations.idiomatic: I have read the memorial of General Huan Wen, in which he writes that he will personally lead the three hosts, destroy the two rebels, scour the Yellow and Wei valleys and cleanse the old capital, then let the imperial banners sweep like lightning, cross the river in court regalia, restore the throne to the central plain, and set the celestial pivot aright.

sentences.zh: 」斯超世之弘圖，千載之盛事。

translations.literal: " This is a transcending generation's great plan, a thousand years' splendid affair.
translations.idiomatic: " That would be a plan to tower above the age and a deed to shine for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 然臣之所懷，竊有未安，以為帝王之興，莫不藉地利人和以建功業，貴能以義平暴，因而撫之。

translations.literal: Yet what your subject cherishes in the breast, privately has what is not settled; I hold that emperors' and kings' rise, none did not rely on terrain's advantage and men's harmony to establish merit and enterprise, valuing able by righteousness to pacify violence, thereby to soothe them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in my heart something still troubles me: every founder of a dynasty has relied on favorable terrain and the support of the people to build his work, and has prized the use of justice to crush violence and then to comfort those he conquers.

sentences.zh: 懷湣不建，滄胥秦京，遂令胡戎交侵，神州絕綱，土崩之釁，誠由道喪。

translations.literal: Huai and Min not established, sank to Qin capital; thereupon caused Hu and Rong mutually to encroach, the divine continent's net snapped; earth-collapse's blame, truly from the Way's loss.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperors Huai and Min could not hold the house, the capital fell to ruin and barbarian hosts overran one another; the bonds of the Chinese world snapped, and the landslide came because the moral order had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 然中夏蕩蕩，一時橫流，百郡千城曾無完郛者，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet the central Xia vast and empty, at one time flowing sideways, hundred commanderies thousand cities ever without intact inner walls—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the heartland was swept bare in a single flood; of hundreds of commanderies and thousands of towns scarcely one kept its walls whole—why was that?

sentences.zh: 亦以地不可守，投奔有所故也。

translations.literal: Also because the ground could not be defended, fleeing and casting oneself had a reason.
translations.idiomatic: Because the land could no longer be defended and the people had to flee somewhere.

sentences.zh: 天祚未革，中宗龍飛，非惟信順協於天人而已，實賴萬里長江畫而守之耳。

translations.literal: Heaven's blessing not yet changed, Zhongzong dragon-soared—not only trust and compliance harmonized with Heaven and man, but truly relied on the ten-thousand-li Yangtze drawn and guarded.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate had not yet passed from Jin; Emperor Yuan rose like a dragon—not only because trust and obedience ran with Heaven and men, but because he could draw the line of defense along the long Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 《易》稱「王公設險以守其國」，險之時義大矣哉！

translations.literal: The Changes states, "The king and duke set peril to guard their state"—peril's timely meaning is great indeed!
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says that kings and dukes set natural barriers to defend their states—how great is the meaning of "peril" in its season!

sentences.zh: 斯已然之明效也。

translations.literal: This is already realized clear effect.
translations.idiomatic: That lesson is already plain in our own experience.

sentences.zh: 今作勝談，自當任道而遺險；

translations.literal: Now making victory talk, naturally ought to entrust the Way and cast aside peril;
translations.idiomatic: In fine rhetoric one may trust the Way and forget about terrain;

sentences.zh: 校實量分，不得不保小以固存。

translations.literal: comparing reality and measuring share, cannot but preserve the small to firm existence.
translations.idiomatic: yet when one weighs the facts, one must cling to what can be held if the state is to survive.

sentences.zh: 自喪亂已來六十餘年，蒼生殄滅，百不遺一，河洛丘、虛，函夏蕭條，井堙木刊，阡陌夷滅，生理茫茫，永無依歸。

translations.literal: Since disorder and chaos more than sixty years, dark life perished and destroyed, of hundred not one left; He and Luo mounds and void, Huanxia desolate; wells buried, trees cut; paths and fields leveled and extinguished; life's principle vast and boundless, forever without reliance and return.
translations.idiomatic: More than sixty years have passed since the catastrophe; the common folk were slaughtered until fewer than one in a hundred remained; the Yellow and Luo valleys are heaped ruins, the heartland is empty, wells are choked and groves felled, field paths gone—there is no livelihood there and no home to return to.

sentences.zh: 播流江表，已經數世，存者長子老孫，亡者丘隴成行。

translations.literal: Scattered and flowed south of the river, already passed several generations; the living have grown sons and aged grandsons; the dead have mound lines in rows.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fled south of the Yangtze have lived there for generations; the living have raised sons and grandsons, and the dead lie in ranked tombs.

sentences.zh: 雖北風之思感其素心，目前之哀實為交切。

translations.literal: Although the north wind's longing touches their plain hearts, the present eye's grief is truly mutually cutting.
translations.idiomatic: They still feel the north wind's pull in their hearts, yet the grief before their eyes cuts them to the quick.

sentences.zh: 若遷都旋軫之日，中舉五陵，即復緬成遐域。

translations.literal: If on the day of moving the capital and turning the chariot, within raising the five tombs, then again becomes distant region.
translations.idiomatic: If the court wheels north and the capital moves, the imperial tombs at Wuling will at once lie beyond a distant frontier.

sentences.zh: 泰山之安既難以理保，烝烝之思豈不纏於聖心哉！

translations.literal: Mount Tai's peace is already hard to secure by reason; the steaming-steaming longing—how could it not twine in the sagely heart!
translations.idiomatic: The peace of Mount Tai would then be hard to guarantee by any policy, and the tender tie of filial grief could not fail to weigh on Your Majesty's heart!

sentences.zh: 溫今此舉，誠欲大覽始終，為國遠圖。

translations.literal: Wen's now this act, truly desires greatly to survey beginning and end, for the state's distant plan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's present plan does aim to see the whole course through and to work a lasting good for the state.

sentences.zh: 向無山陵之急，亦未首決大謀，獨任天下之至難也。

translations.literal: If there had not been the tombs' urgency, also would not have first decided the great plan, alone undertaking all under Heaven's utmost difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Had there been no crisis at the imperial tombs, he would not have pressed so bold a design or taken on alone the hardest task in the realm.

sentences.zh: 今發憤忘食，忠慨亮到，凡在有心，孰不致感！

translations.literal: Now rousing resentment forgetting food, loyal indignation bright and reaching—all who have a heart, who does not reach feeling!
translations.idiomatic: Now he forgets his meals in loyal zeal, and every feeling heart is moved!

sentences.zh: 而百姓震駭，同懷危懼者，豈不以反舊之樂賒，而趣死之憂促哉！

translations.literal: Yet the hundred surnames quake in alarm, together cherishing danger and fear—is it not because returning to the old's joy is distant, while hastening to death's worry is pressing!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people are terrified and share a single dread—because the joy of going home is still far off while the fear of marching to death is immediate!

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: What is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 植根于江外數十年矣，一朝拔之，頓驅踧於空荒之地，提挈萬里，逾險浮深，離墳墓，棄生業，富者無三年之糧，貧者無一餐之飯，田宅不可復售，舟車無從而得，舍安樂之國，適習亂之鄉，出必安之地，就累卵之危，將頓僕道塗，飄溺江川，僅有達者。

translations.literal: They have planted roots beyond the Yangtze for decades; in one morning to uproot them, suddenly to drive and press into empty waste lands, leading and carrying ten thousand li, crossing peril and floating depth, leaving tombs, abandoning livelihoods; the rich lack three years' grain, the poor lack one meal's rice; fields and houses cannot again be sold, boats and carts have no way to be obtained; leaving happy and peaceful lands, going to accustomed-to-chaos villages; exiting must-be-safe ground, approaching piled-eggs' peril—will stumble and fall on the roads, drift and drown in river streams; only a few will reach.
translations.idiomatic: They have set down roots south of the river for decades; to tear them up at a stroke and march them into a barren wilderness, dragging families a thousand miles over peril and deep water, leaving ancestral graves and livelihoods—the rich have not grain for three years, the poor not a meal in the pot; they cannot sell their lands or find carts and boats; they would leave a peaceful country for a land of chronic war, step from safety into danger piled as high as eggs, stumble and die on the road or drown in the rivers, and only a handful would arrive.

sentences.zh: 夫國以人為本，疾寇所以為人，眾喪而寇除，亦安所取裁？

translations.literal: Now the state takes people as root; hating bandits is for people's sake; if the masses perish and the bandits are removed, where then is the taking of measure?
translations.idiomatic: The state exists for its people; we hate the invaders because they harm the people—if the people are destroyed while the invaders are cleared, what victory is left to measure?

sentences.zh: 此仁者所宜哀矜，國家所宜深慮也。

translations.literal: This is what benevolent men ought pity; what the state ought deeply consider.
translations.idiomatic: This is what a humane ruler must pity and what the court must weigh with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 自古今帝王之都，豈有常所，時隆則宅中而圖大，勢屈則遵養以待會。

translations.literal: From ancient to present emperors' and kings' capitals, how could there be a constant place? When the times rise high then dwell in the center and plan great; when power bends low then follow and nurture awaiting the meeting.
translations.idiomatic: Capitals have never been fixed for all time: when fortune is high the court sits in the center and plans on a grand scale; when power is weak it withdraws and bides its time for the right moment.

sentences.zh: 使德不可勝，家有三年之積，然後始可謀太平之事耳。

translations.literal: Cause virtue to be invincible, every house to have three years' store—only then may one begin to plan great peace's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue must be more than a match for any foe, and every household must have three years' grain in store before one may speak of lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 今天時人事，有未至者矣，一朝欲一宇宙，無乃頓而難舉乎？

translations.literal: Now Heaven's season and human affairs have what has not yet arrived; in one morning desiring to unify the cosmos—is this not abrupt and hard to raise?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's timing and human readiness have not yet met; to try to set the whole world in order at a single stroke—is that not rash and beyond our strength?

sentences.zh: 臣之愚計，以為且可更遣一將有威名資實者，先鎮洛陽，於陵所築二壘以奉衛山陵，掃平梁、許，清一河南，運漕之路既通，然後盡力於開墾，廣田積穀，漸為徙者之資。

translations.literal: Your subject's foolish plan thinks that for the nonce one may again dispatch a general who has awe-inspiring name and solid substance, first to garrison Luoyang, at the tombs' place build two forts to serve and guard the imperial tombs, sweep and pacify Liang and Xu, clear and unify south of the River; when transport and canal's road is already open, then exhaust strength in opening wasteland, widening fields and piling grain, gradually providing capital for those who move.
translations.idiomatic: My humble plan would be to send first a seasoned general of proven reputation to hold Luoyang, raise twin forts at the tomb precinct to guard the imperial graves, clear the Liang and Xu regions and pacify the south bank of the Yellow River, open the grain barges again, and only then push reclamation, widen the fields, and pile up grain as a fund for gradual resettlement.

sentences.zh: 如此，賊見亡征，勢必遠竄。

translations.literal: If thus, the bandits seeing omens of perishing, their situation must flee far.
translations.idiomatic: Then the enemy will read the signs of doom and scatter far away.

sentences.zh: 如其迷逆不化，復欲送死者，南北諸軍風馳電赴，若身手之救痛癢，率然之應首尾，山陵既固，中夏小康。

translations.literal: If they are deluded and rebellious, not transformed, again desiring to send death, then north and south various armies wind-run lightning-arrive, like hand and body's saving itch and pain, suddenly responding head and tail; the tombs already firm, central Xia small peace.
translations.idiomatic: If they cling to rebellion and court death again, the armies north and south can strike like wind and lightning, head and tail answering like hand to itch; the tombs will stand secure and the heartland will know a measure of peace.

sentences.zh: 陛下且端委紫極，增修德政，躬行漢文簡樸之至，去小惠，節游費，審官人，練甲兵，以養士滅寇為先。

translations.literal: Your Majesty for the nonce correct and draped at the purple pole, increase and cultivate virtuous government, personally practice Han Wendi's simplicity's utmost, remove small favors, curtail roaming expense, examine office men, drill armor and weapons, taking nurturing knights and destroying bandits as first.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Your Majesty may sit serene on the throne, deepen virtuous rule, follow Emperor Wen of Han in plain living, cut petty largess and pleasure travel, scrutinize appointments, drill the hosts, and put the feeding of the army and the destruction of the enemy first.

sentences.zh: 十年行之，無使隳廢，則貧者殖其財，怯者充其勇，人知天德，赴死如歸，以此致政，猶運諸掌握。

translations.literal: Ten years practice it, do not let it fall and waste, then the poor increase their wealth, the timid fill their courage; men know Heaven's virtue, rush to death like returning home; by this to achieve government is still like turning it in the palm's grasp.
translations.idiomatic: Pursue this for ten years without slackening, and the poor will grow rich, the timid grow brave, men will feel Heaven's kindness and go to death as gladly as home—then good government rests in the palm of your hand.

sentences.zh: 何故舍百勝之長理，舉天下而一擲哉！

translations.literal: What reason to abandon hundred-victories' long principle, lifting all under Heaven and one throw!
translations.idiomatic: Why abandon a strategy sure to win and stake the whole realm on a single throw!

sentences.zh: 陛下春秋方富，溫克壯其猷，君臣相與，弘養德業，括囊元吉，豈不快乎！

translations.literal: Your Majesty's spring and autumn are just rich; Wen is able to strengthen his plans; lord and ministers mutually together, enlarge and nurture virtue's enterprise, tie the sack's great good—how could it not be joyful!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is in the prime of life and Huan Wen in the vigor of his plans; ruler and minister together can build virtue and hold fortune in the bag like the hexagram's great good—could anything be more welcome!

sentences.zh: 今溫唱高議，聖朝互同，臣以輕微，獨獻管見。

translations.literal: Now Wen initiates high discourse, the sagely court mutually concurs; your subject by slight and humble alone offers tube's seeing.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen has set forth his lofty proposal and the court echoes him; I alone, the least of your servants, offer the view through a narrow tube.

sentences.zh: 出言之難，實在今日，而臣區區必聞天聽者，竊以無諱之朝，狂瞽進說，芻蕘之謀，聖賢所察，所以不勝至憂，觸冒幹陳。

translations.literal: Issuing words' difficulty is truly in this day; yet your subject in petty certainty must reach Heaven's hearing—privately holding that in a court without taboo, the mad and blind advance speech; fodder-cutters' plans, sages and worthies examine; therefore unable to bear utmost worry, I offend and risk to state plainly.
translations.idiomatic: To speak out is hardest at a moment like this, yet I must reach Your Majesty's ear because in an age that welcomes frank counsel even the blind may speak and sages weigh the woodcutter's plan—such is the depth of my fear that I risk offense to lay it bare.

sentences.zh: 若陛下垂神，溫少留思，豈非屈於一人而允億兆之顧哉！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty lets fall spirit, Wen slightly retains thought—is it not bending to one man while granting the hundred millions' hope!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will bend an ear and Huan Wen pause to reflect, would that not mean yielding a little to one man while granting the wish of millions!

sentences.zh: 如以幹忤罪大，欲加顯戮，使丹誠上達，退受刑誅，雖沒泉壤，屍且不朽。

translations.literal: If because of offense by importunity the crime is great, desiring to add manifest execution—yet let red sincerity ascend and reach, then withdraw and receive punishment and execution; although sunk in spring and soil, the corpse will still not rot.
translations.idiomatic: If my bluntness counts as a great crime and Your Majesty would have me executed openly, let this loyal heart first be heard; I will then withdraw and accept death, and though I sink into the earth my bones will not rot.

sentences.zh: 桓溫見綽表，不悅，曰：「致意興公，何不尋君《遂初賦》，知人家國事邪！

translations.literal: Huan Wen saw Chuo's memorial, was not pleased, said: "Convey my meaning to Xinggong—why not pursue your Rhapsody on Finding Life's First Intent, and meddle in others' state affairs!
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen read Sun Chuo's memorial without pleasure and said, "Give Xinggong my word: why does he not stick to his rhapsody On Finding Life's First Intent instead of prying into another man's statecraft!"

sentences.zh: 」尋轉廷尉卿，領著作。

translations.literal: " Soon he was transferred to commandant of justice, concurrently composition.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward Sun Chuo was made commandant of justice while retaining charge of the editorial office.

sentences.zh: 綽少以文才垂稱，于時文士，綽為其冠。

translations.literal: Chuo in youth by literary talent hung fame; among the time's literary scholars, Chuo was their cap.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuo won fame early as a writer and stood at the head of the literary men of his day.

sentences.zh: 溫、王、郗、庾諸公之薨，必須綽為碑文，然後刊石焉。

translations.literal: When Wen, Wang, Xi, Yu various lords died, it was necessary for Chuo to compose the stele text, and only then was stone carved.
translations.idiomatic: When great men such as Huan Wen, Wang Dao, Xi Jian, and Yu Liang died, Sun Chuo had to draft the inscription before the stele could be cut.

sentences.zh: 年五十八，卒。

translations.literal: Age fifty-eight, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子嗣，有綽風，文章相亞，位至中軍參軍，早亡。

translations.literal: Son Si, had Chuo's wind; their writings mutually seconded; rank reached Central Army army adviser; died early.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Si resembled his father in manner and ran him close as a writer; he rose to army adviser on the staff of the central army but died young.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：江統風檢操行，良有可稱，陳留多士，斯為其冠。

translations.literal: The historian says: Jiang Tong's bearing, scrutiny, and conduct truly have what may be praised; among Chenliu's many scholars, he was their cap.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: In demeanor and conduct Jiang Tong had much to commend, and among the many talents of Chenliu he stood first.

sentences.zh: 《徙戎》之論，實乃經國遠圖。

translations.literal: The "Relocation of the Rong" discourse is truly a governing-the-state distant plan.
translations.idiomatic: His treatise on relocating the Rong was statesmanship of the longest view.

sentences.zh: 然運距中衰，陵替有漸，假其言見用，恐速禍招怨，無救於將顛也。

translations.literal: Yet fortune opposed mid-decline, tombs' replacement had gradualness; if his words had been used, I fear would hasten disaster and summon resentment, not saving the about-to-topple.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fate had set the dynasty on a slope of decline; had his advice been followed, it might only have hastened disaster and rancor and could not have saved the house as it tottered.

sentences.zh: 逮湣懷廢徙，冒禁拜辭，所謂命輕鴻毛，義貴熊掌。

translations.literal: When it reached Min and Huai's deposal and removal, braving prohibition to bow farewell—this is what is called life light as swan feather, righteousness precious as bear paw.
translations.idiomatic: When Princes Min and Huai were deposed and banished, he broke the ban to bid them farewell—life light as a goose feather, duty weighty as a bear's paw.

sentences.zh: 虨位隆端石，竭誠獻替。

translations.literal: Bin's position was lofty at the pillar stone; he exhausted loyalty in offering removal.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Bin rose to the summit of the civil service and gave his utmost in counsel for the good of the throne.

sentences.zh: 惇遺忽榮利，聿修天爵。

translations.literal: Dun cast aside and neglected glory and profit, thereby cultivating Heaven's noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Dun turned his back on rank and gain and cultivated the nobility that Heaven grants.

sentences.zh: 雖出處異途，俱難兄弟矣。

translations.literal: Although emerging and dwelling were different paths, both were hard as brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Though they took different paths in and out of office, both brothers were men hard to match.

sentences.zh: 孫楚體英絢之姿，超然出類，見知武子，誠無愧色。

translations.literal: Sun Chu embodied heroic and splendid bearing, transcendent beyond his class; seen and known by Wu Zi—truly without shameful color.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chu bore a brilliant presence and stood above the common run; that Wang Ji recognized him was no discredit to either man.

sentences.zh: 覽其貽皓之書，諒曩代之佳筆也。

translations.literal: Reading his letter left to Hao, truly it is a past generation's fine brush.
translations.idiomatic: To read his letter to Sun Hao is to see one of the finest pens of an earlier age.

sentences.zh: 而負才誕傲，蔑苞忿奕，違遜讓之道，肆陵憤之氣，丁年沈廢，諒自取矣。

translations.literal: Yet relying on talent he was wildly arrogant, despised Bao and resented Yi, violated yielding and deferring's way, unleashed bullying and indignant qi; in prime years sunk and discarded—truly he brought it on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he trusted his gifts to the point of arrogance, slighted Shi Bao and quarreled with Guo Yi, spurned modesty, and gave free rein to his haughty temper, so that he languished in his prime—he had himself to blame.

sentences.zh: 統、綽棣華秀髮，名顯中興，可謂無忝爾祖。

translations.literal: Tong and Chuo, dihua splendid hair, name displayed in the restoration—can be called not shaming your ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tong and Sun Chuo, like flowering catalpa, won fame in the restoration and did no dishonor to their forebears.

sentences.zh: 統竟淪跡下邑，窮觀勝地，會其心焉。

translations.literal: Tong in the end sank his traces in lower towns, exhaustively viewing winning places, meeting his heart there.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tong ended his days in a humble magistracy, roaming every famous landscape until his heart found rest.

sentences.zh: 綽獻直論辭，都不懾元子，有匪躬之節，豈徒文雅而已哉！

translations.literal: Chuo presented straight-discourse phrases, wholly not fearing Yuanzi—having not-for-self body's integrity; how only literary elegance!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuo set forth blunt remonstrance without flinching before Huan Wen and showed the integrity of a man who forgets himself for his lord—far more than mere literary grace!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：應元蹈義，子荊越俗。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Yingyuan treads righteousness; Zijing surpasses custom.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium runs: Jiang Tong trod the path of duty; Sun Chu rose above the vulgar.

sentences.zh: 江寡悔尤，孫貽擯辱。

translations.literal: Jiang had few regrets and faults; Sun brought casting-aside shame.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangs knew few regrets; the Suns brought exile and shame on themselves.

sentences.zh: 統昆弟，江左馳聲。

translations.literal: Tong and brothers, east of the Yangtze raced fame.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tong and his brothers won renown east of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 彬彬藻思，綽冠群英。

translations.literal: Refined and patterned thought, Chuo capped the host of heroes.
translations.idiomatic: In polished literary genius Sun Chuo stood first among the outstanding men of his time.
